systems.name: mintburn
systems.summary: The orchestrator for Anchorage-issued stablecoins and tokenized assets: it owns the durable state machines for minting, burning, bridging, swapping, tokenization, manual fiat deposits, reserves reporting and stablecoin smart-contract operations, and delegates every actual asset move to other services.
purpose: mintburn runs the full lifecycle of Anchorage-issued stablecoins and tokenized assets. Everything it does is a durable Temporal workflow over its own Postgres state machines: issue/redeem (fiat in, token minted; token burned, fiat out), BRIDGE (cross-chain burn-then-mint over LayerZero), SWAP (cross-issuer conversion with reserve rebalancing), Coinductor event-driven automation, single-leg tokenization, operator-recorded manual fiat deposits, scheduled reserves-composition ingestion, and roughly sixty smart-contract operations against the token contracts and their LayerZero wiring.

It is not a custodian and it does not touch chains or banks directly. Wallets, operations, holds, balances and accounting come from custody; on-chain submission from blockchain; fiat rails from bankadapter; automated endorsement from autopengateway (the legacy deployment today, the Stablecoins CVM deployment behind a migration flag). Chain reads go through rpc-lib (EVM and SVM only) and LayerZero pathway configuration through lzconfig.

Three groups of consumers call it. Issuers reach it through the issuer dashboard and its Porto BFF, over REST v2 and gRPC. Customers reach it through REST v2 and the federated GraphQL graph, where mintburn serves its own subgraph on :8082. Operations staff reach it through Retool. Other services read from it too: boton for conversion history, custodystatements, readonlyapi as the REST v2 proxy, and autopengateway for cross-check and augmentation policies.

domains.name: Issue/redeem (including bridge and swap)
domains.summary: The core conversion domain. A mint takes fiat and issues token; a burn takes token and returns fiat. BRIDGE is a cross-chain burn-then-mint over LayerZero. SWAP is a cross-issuer conversion that also rebalances reserves, with the reserve-transfer endorsement signed via Cloud KMS in production.

domains.name: Coinductor
domains.summary: Event-driven automation. A customer's quorum endorses a MINT or BURN policy; afterwards a custody deposit event triggers a conversion automatically, and the policy may optionally include an automated withdrawal to a trusted destination. Coinductor withdrawals carry a structured amlproto submission for travel-rule reporting.

domains.name: Tokenization
domains.summary: Single-leg mint or burn of tokenized assets - tokenized_deposit and tokenized_gold - without the fiat leg of issue/redeem.

domains.name: Manual deposit
domains.summary: Fiat deposits that operators observe and record by hand (FEDWIRE, SWIFT, CHIPS or BOOK). Each one needs operator quorum approval and is then pushed to bankadapter.

domains.name: Reserves composition
domains.summary: A Temporal schedule pulls reserve attestation data out of BigQuery three times a day, stores the composition history, raises a Slack alert when the reserve ratio looks anomalous, and backs the public reserves REST endpoints.

domains.name: Smart-contract operations
domains.summary: Roughly sixty gRPC operations against the deployed token contracts: pause and block controls, role grants, proxy upgrades, and the LayerZero OFT adapter, Endpoint, ULN and DVN configuration.

domains.name: Stablecoins and chains
domains.summary: Coin roster bundled as metadata: USDtb (Ethena, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank), USDGO (OSL), USDPT (Western Union) and USDX (test). The reserves pipeline covers USDGO, USDtb, USDPT, fUSD and ZLUSD from BigQuery tables anc-global-analytics.stablecoin_issuance.<coin>_stablecoin_recon. Production issuer orgs are ADB Stablecoin Issuer, ADB-NA USAT Issuer and OSL Group; USAT is a third-party LayerZero adapter with its own ISSUE_USAT/REDEEM_USAT operation types. Chain support is EVM and SVM only through rpc-lib (Ethereum mainnet/Hoodi, Solana mainnet/devnet, Arbitrum mainnet/regnet, BSC mainnet/testnet), with the networks config loaded from a Secret Manager JSON blob. LayerZero pathways come from lzconfig per environment: production ethereum (endpoint 30101, USDX plus third-party HADRON_USDX and USAT), bsc (30102, USDX) and celo (30125, third-party); staging and development use hoodi to bsc-testnet with USDX; local uses anvil plus arbitrum-regnet with USDX7.

systems.name: stablecoins-autopen / autopengateway
systems.summary: autopengateway (the Go service at source/go/service/autopengateway) and stablecoins-autopen (the deployed Ironclave TDX confidential VM and the Datadog service name) are the same binary, an automated endorser that signs low-risk stablecoin execute operations so issuance needs no human quorum per operation.
purpose: The gateway programmatically endorses low-risk execute operations: execute.Generic operations for stablecoin mint and burn (live) and execute.Withdraw operations for Coinductor automated withdrawals (built, but denied in production). Without it, every mint and burn would need a human quorum endorsement on the custody operation before the chain transaction could be signed. It is not a custodian and holds no customer keys; it only adds one endorsement to an operation custody has already put into SIGS_REQUIRED, and only after an ordered policy chain agrees.

It signs with a single attested identity. An ephemeral Ed25519 key is generated inside the CVM by see-runner and handed to the process on stdin together with an X.509 chain whose leaf is issued by the HSM and lives 48 hours. Endorsements are submitted to custody through EndorseOperationWithCert: the gateway builds a CertEndorsementPayload{OperationID, APPROVE, EndorsedParamsDigest}, signs its canonical form, and attaches the DER certificate chain. The outbound call to custody carries no caller-identity auth, so authorization rests entirely on verifying that certificate-embedded signature (README Open Risk 6), and the HSM re-checks the same decision at sign time.

The host is Ironclave, Anchorage's confidential-computing platform: Intel TDX Confidential VMs with secure boot, vTPM and remote attestation, running a measured UKI (unified kernel image) whose measurements the HSM must have approved before it will issue any credential. Three Ironclave tenants share the platform today: hsm-native, stablecoins-autopen and cvm-privacy-ristretto.

domains.name: Policy chain
domains.summary: An ordered pipeline evaluated before signing; the first non-nil error denies and short-circuits. Always-on stages: token-type, op-classification, amount-resolver, irc-augmentation, asset-config-augmentation, mintburn-cross-check, coinductor-run-augmentation, coinductor-cross-check. Configurable gates come from ANCHOR_POLICY_ADAPTERS: organization-allowlist, per-kind-allowlist (asset per operation kind), per-kind max amount, rolling-window-cap (24h mint+burn total). An empty chain denies everything and an empty configured adapter list is refused at startup. A 2026-08-20 redesign is expected to merge the front of the chain into op-classification, asset-resolution and mintburn-cross-check, so these stage names may change: see gap-autopen-policy-chain-redesign.

domains.name: Trust model
domains.summary: The signing key is bound to an attestation: CVM_BOOTSTRAP_MODE selects CVMSigner, which accepts only the key and chain see-runner passes on stdin, with no PEM fallback in deployed environments, so the signer fails closed. Rotation invariant: the leaf lives 48h, a jittered SIGTERM at about 40h restarts the boot loop for a fresh attestation, and signing refuses when under 7h of validity remains (ErrCertNearExpiry) - 40h + 7h must stay under 48h. Policy is enforced twice: the gateway chain, then the HSM at sign time (source/c/hsm/vsp/autoendorse.cpp checks the organization allowlist, decision == APPROVE and the endorsedParamsDigest binding), so the two allowlists must be kept in sync. Audit-log reservation makes the cap safe: a global endorsement lock, then decide, then write a PROCESSING row before signing, then finalize; a crash leaves PROCESSING counting toward the cap (conservative), and denials are written DEFERRED and do not count. Only mintburn dials the CVM, and the CVM does not hold the backend userauth signing keyset.

systems.name: Botón
systems.summary: Independent on-chain observer that watches Anchorage-owned smart contracts through Hexagate webhooks, pages incident.io when on-chain activity cannot be reconciled against internal records, and can pull the LayerZero bridge kill switch by calling Pause on bridgingauthorizer.
purpose: Botón verifies on-chain activity for both stablecoin markets. On the primary market it takes every mint and burn observed on an allowlisted token contract and reconciles it against two internal records: the Custody execute operation for the transaction hash, and the mintburn issue/redeem record for that operation id. On the secondary market it takes LayerZero bridge events, classifies the (contract, event) pair against the Role x Impact response matrix, and turns the verdict into a page and/or a global bridge pause.

It exists because every other check in the stablecoin path is made by the same systems that create the operations. Botón reads the chain from the outside (via Hexagate) and compares what actually happened to what Anchorage believes it did, so a mint that no internal record explains gets a human on it. On the secondary market it also provides containment, not just detection: for the highest-impact bridge events it pauses the bridging authorizer without waiting for a human, because the page is slower than an unbounded mint.

Nothing inside the monorepo calls Botón. It has no ClusterIP service, no gRPC surface and no GraphQL subgraph; its only inbound traffic is Hexagate webhooks arriving through a public GKE Gateway. The set of Hexagate monitors that feed it is configured by hand in the Hexagate UI and is not declared in this repo, so the repo cannot tell you what Botón is currently watching (see gap-boton-hexagate-monitors-manual).

domains.name: Primary-market validation
domains.summary: Mint and burn calls on allowlisted token contracts are reconciled against Custody (GetExecuteOperationForTxReceiptID, GetWalletAddress) and mintburn (GetIssueRedeemHistory). The MintBurnValidation workflow polls Custody for up to 13 attempts across roughly 24 hours, looks the issue/redeem record up over a 7-day window, then runs three checks (operation-type pairing, counterparty address, amount) and alerts incident.io on any discrepancy.

domains.name: Secondary-market bridge evaluation
domains.summary: LayerZero bridge events are resolved to a monitored contract via the BridgeContractRegistry built by lzconfig.Load(env), classified by the (contract, event) response matrix, and turned into a page and/or a call to bridgingauthorizer Pause. Contract roles are SendUln302, ReceiveUln302 and EndpointV2 (chain-wide) plus OFTAdapter, ProxyAdmin and DVN (token-scoped, with dvnType test-token or production-token).

domains.name: Response matrix
domains.summary: The catalog in classify.go holds 12 cases: SecurityStackConfigChange, VerificationMessageAnomaly, UpgradeAuthorityAnomaly, AdminRoleAnomaly, FeeConfigAnomaly, RateLimitConfigAnomaly, PauseAnomaly, DVNAttestationAnomaly, DVNRoleAnomaly, DVNAdminRotation, DVNConfigAnomaly and DVNProbing. Each row carries a blast radius, ordered Liveness < LivenessOutbound < Malicious < CriticalUnboundedMint, and a tier: T0 goes to the bridging on-call, T1 to a broader audience, and both page today. Only three rows do not page at all: the DVN VerifySignaturesFailed, HashAlreadyUsed and ExecuteFailed rows, which are count-only (LogWarn plus the boton.bridge.events counter). Unconditional auto-pause rows are the EndpointV2 InboundNonceSkipped, PacketBurnt and fc:clear rows; PacketNilified is reversible, so it is T1 and never pauses, and rate-limit config changes page without pausing because the authorizer has its own pre-sign rate check. DVN RoleAdminChanged, Paused and Unpaused are should-never-fire canaries: they exist so that a change nobody expects still reaches a human.

systems.name: stablecoinrewards
systems.summary: Runs Anchorage stablecoin reward programs: it enrolls participants, aggregates daily yield from BigQuery into monthly payouts, and pays them out as Settlement Network transfers.
purpose: stablecoinrewards (often shortened to SCR) owns four things. Programs: a named reward program with a start date, a set of eligible stablecoin asset types and a status, created and approved by staff. Participants: one participant row per top-level affiliate, strictly 1:1, holding the link to that affiliate Atlas participant (Atlas is the Settlement Network participant/vault model). Payouts: one row per participant, program and payout month, carrying the amount and a status. Asset rates: the latest reference and effective reward rate per stablecoin, refreshed daily from a BigQuery reporting table so the dashboard can show a rate without querying BigQuery on the read path.

The identity chain the service walks is Organization -> Accounts (resolved through the KYC service) -> Affiliates -> Top-level affiliates -> Atlas participants. Because participants are 1:1 with top-level affiliates, one organization with several top-level affiliates becomes several participants. Enrollment happens three ways: manual (staff enroll one top-level affiliate from the Stablecoin Rewards Onboarding Retool app), self-serve (an organization user accepts terms in the Client Dashboard, which starts the EnrollOrganization workflow and records the org in org_enrollments), and automatic (a daily cron re-walks every org in org_enrollments and creates participants for top-level affiliates that appeared since the last run). Only top-level affiliates in an approved jurisdiction are eligible; the allow-list is per environment and is the single most common cause of a client not seeing the rewards page.

The payout model is deliberately split into a staff-driven pipeline. Daily per-affiliate yield is produced upstream and lands in BigQuery (anc-global-analytics.stables_yield.fct_yield_client_data). Staff press Generate Payouts in the Payouts Retool app, which runs a workflow that reads the daily rows for a month, aggregates them per participant and program, and writes PENDING payout rows (intra-org payouts, where sender and receiver Atlas participants are the same, are written SKIPPED for the operations team to handle by hand). Staff then press Submit Payouts, which fans out one child workflow per pending payout; each child creates a two-way settlement in the Settlement Network and then waits for Pub/Sub settlement events to drive the payout to a final state. The service never touches a chain RPC: the on-chain leg belongs to Settlement Network and custody.

Temporal worker is deliberately throttled: 4 workflow-task pollers + 4 activity-task pollers and 16 concurrent workflow + 16 concurrent activity execution slots, against library defaults of 40+40 pollers and 1000 slots each, with the SDK deadlock-detection timeout widened from 1s to 3s.

Why: the pod runs on a small CPU quota, and the 16:00 UTC enrollment fan-out pulled work proportional to orgs x affiliates. That starved the workflow goroutines of scheduler time past the SDK wall-clock deadlock budget and surfaced as intermittent TMPRL1101 potential deadlock workflow-task failures. Bounded slots push the excess back onto the Temporal server queue, and the 3s budget absorbs brief CFS throttling.

The same incident drove bounded child batching in internal/temporal/child_fan_out.go: an EnrollOrganization run starts at most 25 EnrollTopLevelAffiliate children at a time, and the auto-enroll cron starts at most 5 EnrollOrganization children at a time, each batch awaited before the next.

The pod carries the label latencyalerts: exempt to opt out of the global 1s latency alerts, and defines custom 45s HTTP and gRPC latency GlobalRules instead, because workflow-starting handlers are legitimately slow.

systems.name: bridgingauthorizer
systems.summary: The DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network) attestation authority that signs LayerZero bridging packets for Anchorage-issued stablecoins. Its source code is NOT in this monorepo — it lives in anchorstablecoins/issuance-systems under services/bridgingauthorizer. What this monorepo holds is only the seams: a hand-synced copy of its control proto (source/shared/protobufs/bridgingauthorizer/v1/bridgingauthorizer.proto), a vendored Go client generated from that copy and used by Botón (source/go/lib/protobufs/bridgingauthorizerproto), DNS-only Terraform for the public hostnames (source/infrastructure/terraform/services/bridgingauthorizer/<env>/dns.tf), a Spacelift stack per environment that applies that DNS (source/infrastructure/terraform/spacelift/stack_bridgingauthorizer.tf), and one Datadog log monitor (source/infrastructure/terraform/datadog-monitors/teams/stablecoins/slo_bridgingauthorizer.tf).
purpose: bridgingauthorizer is Anchorage's DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network) — in LayerZero's security stack a DVN is an off-chain verifier that attests that a cross-chain message really happened, and a destination chain only accepts a packet once the configured DVNs have attested to it. bridgingauthorizer plays that role for Anchorage-issued stablecoin bridging (USDX and similar tokens moving between EVM chains and Solana): it signs/attests LayerZero packets so the destination side can verify them. Its on-chain identity is the per-environment dvnSignerAddress carried in the shared lzconfig data — a secp256k1 signer identity for the DVN committee, not an on-chain account, and it is only meaningful together with that chain's vid (verifier id).

The control surface is deliberately asymmetric: a caller can only ever make the authorizer stop signing (Pause, DenyPacket); it can never make it sign. That is the single most important thing to understand about this service. There is no 'Allow', no 'ApprovePacket', no counterpart to DenyPacket. The worst a compromised or buggy caller can do through the control port is halt bridging — a liveness problem, never a safety one. Pausing is global-only in v1 (no per-token or per-pathway scope), a deliberate simplification with per-pathway pause as a follow-up.

How it relates to the other stablecoins systems: the secondary market (LayerZero bridging) is where bridgingauthorizer AUTHORIZES and Botón WATCHES — Botón classifies suspicious bridge events, pages via incident.io, and pulls the kill switch by calling Pause. The primary market (mint/burn at the contract) is the mirror image: stablecoins-autopen (autopengateway) AUTHORIZES and Botón WATCHES. Botón is the common monitoring plane, and each market has exactly one automated authority Botón can question. The two authorities differ in where their brake lives: autopen's brake is INTERNAL (fail-closed policy chain, audit reservation, 48-hour attested certificate, an HSM second check), while bridgingauthorizer's brake is EXTERNAL — it keeps signing until something outside it, namely Botón, tells it to stop.

It is also a cross-repo boundary. bridgingauthorizer runs in its own GKE cluster (is-production-gke) owned by the issuance-systems infrastructure, with its own public edge projects (anchorsc-is-development / anchorsc-is-staging / anchorsc-is-production). Reading this monorepo tells you how Botón talks to it and what DNS name it answers on; it does not tell you how the service is built, stored, or keyed.

Served only on the gRPC port, never through the external HTTPS gateway.

Its request/response shape, its key handling, and its pre-sign checks all live in anchorstablecoins/issuance-systems and cannot be read from this repo. domains.name: Trust anchors

The data is embedded per environment and immutable at runtime — no mounted file, env var, or dynamic refresh. Separately, the control proto in this repo is a manual copy and must stay byte-identical to the source of truth: gRPC routes on the literal "<package>.<Service>/<Method>" path, so drift breaks the call even when the Go types still compile.

items.name: Pause
items.summary: Pause{reason} stops all signing. Idempotent — pausing while already paused just records the new reason against the same active pause. Global-only in v1: no per-token or per-pathway scope.

items.name: Unpause
items.summary: Unpause{} lifts the pause, if any; a no-op when not paused. A plain v1 handler with no identity hardening yet (STA-1231), and no caller anywhere in this monorepo.

items.name: GetPauseState
items.summary: Reports the current status: {paused, reason, actor, paused_at_unix} — paused_at_unix is 0 when paused is false. No caller in this monorepo.

items.name: DenyPacket
items.summary: DenyPacket{guid (exactly 32 bytes, the LayerZero packet GUID), reason} refuses to ever sign that packet. Permanent in v1: there is no 'allow' counterpart. No caller in this monorepo.

observability.routing: Datadog only; incident.io routing is disabled for this monitor (incidentio_enabled = false).
caveats: There is no SLO. Production traffic is roughly 46 log events per 24 hours with zero errors observed — far too sparse for a rate-based SLI over 15-minute windows, because the denominator is often 0. So the monitor is a plain 'any error in the last hour' log alert rather than a ratio, which is good enough to catch regressions in a low-QPS signing service without generating noise. If and when volume grows the plan is to migrate to a formula-based error-rate query and pair it with an SLO, mirroring slo_autopengateway.tf.

bridgingauthorizer exports only LOGS to Datadog today, unlike boton, mintburn, stablecoinrewards and autopengateway, which are all trace-based. OTLP traces and metrics are wired in anchorstablecoins/issuance-systems PR 153 (STA-1330) but that trace pipeline is not yet steady-state.
The Datadog env tag is stamped by the agent DaemonSet in is-production-gke, not by DD_ENV on the pod.

The Cortex catalog entity for bridgingauthorizer has apm = null and slos = null. Wiring the monitor id into that entity (cortex-catalog/services_stablecoins.tf) is a follow-up: the cortex-catalog stack does not read remote_state from datadog-monitors, so the numeric monitor id has to be hand-wired after the datadog-monitors stack applies. That is why the monitor id is blank here.
The only signal about the authorizer that lives in this monorepo is on Botón's side: the DependencyAuthorizer / "Pause" dependency-request metric emitted around each Pause call.

workflows.name: IssueRedeemConversionRequestHandler

trigger.detail: gRPC MintBurn.CreateIssueRedeem, or REST POST /v2/stablecoins/conversion. Both write the IssueRedeemConversion record first, then start this workflow.

workflows.summary: Front door for every ISSUE, REDEEM, BRIDGE and SWAP conversion: it places the customer hold, creates the off-chain visual-approval operation that collects quorum, starts the long-lived execution child and returns immediately with the two IDs the caller needs.

steps.title: Hold the customer's funds
steps.detail: HoldCustomerFunds asks custody to place a hold for the conversion amount so the balance cannot be spent while the request waits for quorum. A failure here aborts before anything else exists.

branches.then: workflow fails, deferred cancellation handler runs the full cleanup

steps.title: Create the off-chain visual-approval operation
steps.detail: CreateOffchainVisualApprovalSigning asks blockchain for a VISUAL_APPROVAL off-chain operation carrying the human-readable conversion details. OnSignSignaledWorkflowID is set to {issueRedeemID}-request-execution, so when quorum signs, the signal lands on the child, not on this workflow.

steps.title: Start the execution child and wait only for its start
steps.detail: The child IssueRedeemConversionRequestExecution is started with WorkflowID {issueRedeemID}-request-execution, reuse policy ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY and ParentClosePolicy ABANDON so it survives this workflow closing. Only GetChildWorkflowExecution() is awaited, which resolves on start rather than on completion.

branches.then: error is propagated and the deferred handler runs the full cleanup

steps.title: Return the identifiers to the API caller
steps.detail: Returns IssueRedeemID and AuthorizationOperationID. The gRPC and REST handlers block on this result, then (for the API-key path) start AuthorizeConversionFromAPI with the returned AuthorizationOperationID.

steps.title: Full cleanup on cancellation
steps.detail: handleIssueRedeemConversionRequestCancellation runs IssueRedeemConversionRequestFullCleanup (FailOnChainOperation, ReleaseHoldsOnCancellation, FailOffChainOperation) followed by CancelIssueRedeemConversion, which moves the record out of an in-flight state.

branches.then: cleanup always runs

branches.when: only the child was cancelled and the run predates version marker HandleIssueRedeemConversionRequestFailure_FailOffChainOpInParent
branches.then: cleanup is skipped to keep replay deterministic

outcomes.meaning: The request was cancelled before or during quorum collection.
outcomes.rollback: Holds released, on-chain and off-chain operations failed, record moved to a terminal state. Nothing had been minted or burned yet, so there is nothing on chain to undo.

failureHandling: Cleanup runs on a disconnected context via HandleWorkflowCancellation, so it still completes after the workflow context has been cancelled.

RunChildWorkflow returns a *CanceledError raw instead of wrapping it, so a cancelled child routes the parent to CANCELED rather than FAILED. The four permitted termination outcomes are tabulated in .claude/skills/workflow-termination/SKILL.md.
A successful return does not mean the conversion executed: this workflow only guarantees that the hold, the authorization operation and the execution child exist.

workflows.name: IssueRedeemConversionRequestExecution

trigger.detail: Abandoned child of IssueRedeemConversionRequestHandler; it is also the signal target of the off-chain visual-approval operation.

workflows.summary: The quorum gate and dispatcher. It waits for the visual-approval signal, checks the authorization result, runs the (currently hardcoded) issuer review, then dispatches the type-specific operation child and does the post-run bookkeeping.

steps.title: Wait for the quorum signal
steps.detail: Awaits OFFCHAIN_VISUAL_APPROVAL_SIGNING_RESULT, sent by blockchain when the off-chain visual-approval operation reaches a signing decision. The wait has no workflow-level timeout; activity StartToClose is 365 days.

branches.when: the channel closes without a signal (cancellation)
branches.then: returns workflow.ErrCanceled, cancellation cascade runs

steps.title: Check the authorization result
steps.detail: CheckOffchainVisualApprovalSigning reads the resolved authorization operation and reports whether the workflow should stop.

branches.when: ExitEarly (quorum rejected, expired or otherwise not approved)
branches.then: IssueRedeemConversionRequestFullCleanup, record ends REJECTED

steps.title: Issuer review is hardcoded to approve
steps.detail: The Retool-driven issuer review is commented out in code; the workflow instead sets Result=APPROVE, Notes="Automatic approval" and IssuerUserKeyID="system". The ISSUER_WORKFLOW_REVIEW_RESULT channel exists but nothing signals it today, so no human issuer step gates execution. Unconfirmed with the team; see gap-mintburn-issuer-review-auto-approve.

steps.title: Record the issuer decision
steps.detail: CheckIssuerApproval persists the (auto) approval against the conversion record and returns its resulting state.

branches.then: hard error, workflow fails

steps.title: Dispatch the operation child by type
steps.detail: ISSUE to IssueOperation, REDEEM to RedeemOperation, BRIDGE to BridgingOperation, SWAP to SwappingOperation. Children get WorkflowID {issueRedeemID}-{type}-operation, reuse ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY and ParentClosePolicy REQUEST_CANCEL, and are started through the RunChildWorkflow wrapper.

branches.when: operation type is not one of ISSUE, REDEEM, BRIDGE, SWAP
branches.then: error "unsupported operation type"
RunChildWorkflow returns *CanceledError raw so the parent terminates as CANCELED, not FAILED

steps.title: Interpret the child's result string
steps.detail: Anything other than EXECUTED short-circuits the bookkeeping tail.

branches.then: continue to reconciliation
return with no cleanup at all, because the burn already landed on chain and failing the authorization operation would misrepresent it
IssueRedeemConversionRequestPartialCleanup fails only the parent-owned off-chain authorization operation; the child already released holds and failed the on-chain operation

steps.title: Create the reconciliation record
steps.detail: CreateReconciliation writes the reconciliation row that ops and accounting read for the executed conversion.

steps.title: Release the parked authorization operation
steps.detail: The authorization operation was created with DelayCompletion, so it stays in signing until mintburn signals blockchainworkflows.ChannelDelayCompletion for AuthorizationOperationID.

steps.title: Augment the conversion record
steps.detail: AugmentIssueRedeemConversionRecord backfills the derived fields (fees, rates, operation IDs) that reporting and statements consume.

steps.title: Cleanup on cancellation
steps.detail: Same deferred handler as the request handler: full cleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion, on a disconnected context.

outcomes.meaning: The dispatched child reported EXECUTED and the reconciliation, delay-completion release and record augmentation all ran.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to roll back.

outcomes.meaning: Burn landed on chain but the fiat leg failed.
outcomes.rollback: Deliberately nothing: no cleanup, no FailOffChainOperation. The burn is irreversible and ops settle the fiat leg by hand.

outcomes.meaning: The on-chain execute operation exited early because an endorser rejected it.
outcomes.rollback: Child released holds and failed the on-chain operation; parent fails the off-chain authorization operation.

outcomes.meaning: The on-chain operation reached a failed final state.
outcomes.rollback: Child cleanup released holds; parent fails the off-chain authorization operation.

outcomes.meaning: Cancellation reached this workflow or its child.
outcomes.rollback: Full cleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion; anything already confirmed on chain stays.

failureHandling: Cleanup runs on a disconnected context via HandleWorkflowCancellation, so it still completes after the workflow context has been cancelled.

RunChildWorkflow returns a *CanceledError raw instead of wrapping it, so a cancelled child routes the parent to CANCELED rather than FAILED. The four permitted termination outcomes are tabulated in .claude/skills/workflow-termination/SKILL.md.

The parent owns only the off-chain authorization operation. Version marker HandleIssueRedeemConversionRequestFailure_FailOffChainOpInParent moved FailOffChainOperation out of the shared child cleanup into the parent, so runs started before it still fail the off-chain operation inside the child path.

workflows.name: IssueOperation

trigger.detail: Child of IssueRedeemConversionRequestExecution when OperationType is ISSUE. Also used as the mint child of CoinductorAutomationWorkflow.

workflows.summary: Fiat first, mint second. It moves the customer's underlying asset to the issuer, then runs the shared ExecuteOnChainOperationAndWait sub-sequence to create, endorse, confirm and independently validate the mint.

steps.title: Set the record to EXECUTING
steps.detail: SetStateToExecuting flips the conversion record so the API and dashboards stop showing it as merely authorized.

steps.title: Transfer the underlying asset
steps.detail: transferAndWaitForCompletion runs TransferUnderlyingAssetHoldings (version marker UnderlyingAssets; older runs replay the fiat-only TransferFiatHoldings). New executions release the customer hold inside the transfer, before the withdrawal.

steps.title: Wait for the transfer to complete
steps.detail: CheckUnderlyingAssetOperationComplete polls custody every 10 seconds until the transfer operation is terminal.

branches.then: IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup, result ISSUE_UNDERLYING_ASSET_TRANSFER_FAILED. No mint was attempted

steps.title: Release holds (legacy replay path only)
steps.detail: Runs only when GetVersion("ReleaseHoldsMovedIntoTransfer") is below 1, so in-flight runs that recorded an explicit ReleaseHolds activity keep replaying deterministically.

steps.title: Create the mint execute operation
steps.detail: ExecuteOnChainOperationAndWait starts with CreateIssueRedeemExecuteOperation, which asks blockchain for a generic execute operation whose signer is the MinterBurnerRole address from the stablecoin asset configuration, with this workflow as the on-complete signal target.

steps.title: Confirm the operation actually exists
steps.detail: CheckOperationExists guards against a created-but-invisible operation before the workflow commits to waiting for a signal. It retries with backoff and escalates its log to error, reaching Sentry, once the streak passes 15 minutes.

branches.then: error, deferred cleanup

steps.title: Auto-endorse the operation (best effort)
steps.detail: AutoEndorseOperation calls the autopengateway CVM over mTLS. The result is only logged; an endorsement failure never fails the workflow, because a human quorum can still endorse the operation.

branches.then: operation proceeds toward signing
logged only; the operation waits for human endorsement

steps.title: Wait for the on-chain confirmation signal
steps.detail: WaitOnChainOperationFinalState awaits ON_CHAIN_CONFIRMATION, sent by blockchain when the operation reaches a signing/submission decision.

branches.when: the channel closes without a signal
branches.then: result WORKFLOW_CANCELED and workflow.ErrCanceled

steps.title: Verify the operation state
steps.detail: VerifyOnChainOperationState reads the operation back to decide whether to keep waiting for chain finality.

branches.then: result ISSUER_REJECTED

steps.title: Poll to a final on-chain state
steps.detail: PollOnChainOperationFinalState polls until the operation is confirmed or failed on chain.

branches.then: result ON_CHAIN_FAILED

steps.title: Validate the mint against the chain directly
steps.detail: ValidateMintBurnThroughRPC re-reads the mint through rpc-lib (EVM and SVM only) as an independent check that supply actually moved, instead of trusting custody and blockchain alone. Version marker WaitOnChainOperationFinalState_ValidateMintBurnThroughRPC; gated by flag release-mintburn-validate-mint-burn-through-rpc-lib.

branches.then: activity error, deferred cleanup, workflow fails

steps.title: Return the result
steps.detail: EXECUTED when the mint validated. Any non-EXECUTED on-chain result is returned after ExecuteOnChainOperationAndWait has already run IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup.

branches.then: IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup (FailOnChainOperation, ReleaseHoldsOnCancellation) then return that result

steps.title: Cleanup on cancellation
steps.detail: handleIssueRedeemWorkflowCancellation runs IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion on a disconnected context.

outcomes.meaning: Fiat moved, mint confirmed on chain and independently validated through rpc-lib.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to roll back.

outcomes.meaning: The customer's underlying-asset transfer failed before any mint.
outcomes.rollback: Holds released and the on-chain operation failed. No tokens were minted.

outcomes.meaning: An endorser rejected the mint execute operation.
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup released holds and failed the operation, but the fiat leg has already settled to the issuer and is not automatically reversed.

outcomes.meaning: The mint reached a failed final state on chain.
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup released holds and failed the operation; the fiat leg is not automatically reversed.

outcomes.meaning: Cancellation arrived while waiting for the confirmation signal.
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion; a mint already confirmed on chain stays minted.

failureHandling: Cleanup runs on a disconnected context via HandleWorkflowCancellation, so it still completes after the workflow context has been cancelled.

RunChildWorkflow returns a *CanceledError raw instead of wrapping it, so a cancelled child routes the parent to CANCELED rather than FAILED. The four permitted termination outcomes are tabulated in .claude/skills/workflow-termination/SKILL.md.
AutoEndorseOperation is deliberately best-effort: its error is logged by logAutoEndorseResult and swallowed.

sequenceDiagram
  participant W as IssueOperation
  participant C as Custody
  participant B as Blockchain
  participant A as stablecoins-autopen
  participant R as Chain RPC
  W->>C: TransferUnderlyingAssetHoldings
  W->>C: CheckUnderlyingAssetOperationComplete
  C-->>W: complete (else ISSUE_UNDERLYING_ASSET_TRANSFER_FAILED)
  W->>B: CreateIssueRedeemExecuteOperation (mint)
  W->>B: CheckOperationExists
  W->>A: AutoEndorseOperation (best effort)
  A-->>W: ENDORSED / DISABLED / ERRORED
  B-->>W: signal ON_CHAIN_CONFIRMATION
  W->>B: VerifyOnChainOperationState
  W->>B: PollOnChainOperationFinalState
  W->>R: ValidateMintBurnThroughRPC
  R-->>W: mint observed on chain
  W-->>W: EXECUTED

workflows.name: RedeemOperation

trigger.detail: Child of IssueRedeemConversionRequestExecution when OperationType is REDEEM. Also used as the burn child of CoinductorAutomationWorkflow.

workflows.summary: The mirror image of IssueOperation with the order inverted: the burn goes on chain first and the fiat payout follows. Because a burn cannot be undone, a failed fiat leg runs no cleanup at all and is handed to ops.

steps.title: Hold the issuer's funds
steps.detail: HoldIssuerFunds reserves the issuer-side fiat that will pay the customer once the burn lands.

steps.title: Set the record to EXECUTING
steps.detail: SetStateToExecuting flips the conversion record before anything irreversible happens.

steps.title: Create the burn execute operation and check it exists
steps.detail: ExecuteOnChainOperationAndWait runs CreateIssueRedeemExecuteOperation (signer is the asset configuration's MinterBurnerRole) and then CheckOperationExists, with this workflow as the on-complete signal target.

steps.title: Auto-endorse the burn (best effort)
steps.detail: AutoEndorseOperation calls autopengateway over mTLS. For burns the conversion's issuer_funding_operation_id is always still unset at endorsement time, which the endorsement-side policy has to tolerate. Failures are logged only.

branches.then: logged only; the burn waits for human endorsement

steps.title: Await confirmation, verify and poll the burn
steps.detail: WaitOnChainOperationFinalState awaits ON_CHAIN_CONFIRMATION, then VerifyOnChainOperationState and PollOnChainOperationFinalState.

branches.then: result ISSUER_REJECTED, cleanup runs, no fiat is paid
result ON_CHAIN_FAILED, cleanup runs, no fiat is paid
result WORKFLOW_CANCELED

steps.title: Validate the burn against the chain directly
steps.detail: ValidateMintBurnThroughRPC independently re-reads the burn through rpc-lib before the workflow commits to paying fiat.

steps.title: Pay the fiat leg
steps.detail: transferAndWaitForCompletion runs TransferUnderlyingAssetHoldings and CheckUnderlyingAssetOperationComplete. This is the step that happens after, not before, the irreversible on-chain move.

branches.then: return REDEEM_UNDERLYING_ASSET_TRANSFER_FAILED immediately and run no cleanup: the burn already landed, so FailOnChainOperation would fail an operation that actually succeeded. The parent also skips its partial cleanup for this result, leaving the record for ops to settle by hand

steps.title: Release holds (legacy replay path only)
steps.detail: Runs only when GetVersion("ReleaseHoldsMovedIntoTransfer") is below 1; newer runs release the hold inside the transfer.

steps.title: Return EXECUTED
steps.detail: Burn confirmed, validated through rpc-lib and fiat paid.

steps.title: Cleanup on cancellation, but only before the burn lands
steps.detail: handleIssueRedeemWorkflowCancellation runs IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion on a disconnected context. Once the burn has landed the workflow no longer takes the cleanup path for a failed fiat leg: it returns the REDEEM_* result and leaves both the on-chain and the off-chain operation alone.

outcomes.meaning: Burn confirmed and validated, fiat paid to the customer.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to roll back.

outcomes.meaning: Burn landed on chain but the fiat payout failed.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is undone by design. The burn is irreversible, no cleanup runs, the authorization operation is left untouched and ops complete the fiat leg manually.

outcomes.meaning: An endorser rejected the burn execute operation.
outcomes.rollback: Holds released and the on-chain operation failed. No burn, no payout.

outcomes.meaning: The burn reached a failed final state on chain.
outcomes.rollback: Holds released and the on-chain operation failed. No payout.

outcomes.meaning: Cancellation arrived before the burn was confirmed.
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion; a burn already on chain stays burned.

failureHandling: Cleanup runs on a disconnected context via HandleWorkflowCancellation, so it still completes after the workflow context has been cancelled.

RunChildWorkflow returns a *CanceledError raw instead of wrapping it, so a cancelled child routes the parent to CANCELED rather than FAILED. The four permitted termination outcomes are tabulated in .claude/skills/workflow-termination/SKILL.md.

The inverted order is the whole risk model of this workflow: everything after step 5 runs with an irreversible burn already on chain, so the failure paths stop undoing things and start escalating instead.

  W->>B: CreateIssueRedeemExecuteOperation (burn)
  W->>B: CheckOperationExists
