workflows.name: BridgingOperation

trigger.detail: Child of IssueRedeemConversionRequestExecution when OperationType is BRIDGE (cross-chain move over LayerZero).

workflows.summary: Burn on the source chain, mint on the destination chain. There is no fiat leg. The dangerous state is a landed burn with no mint, so every path that can leave that state fires NotifyFailingBridgingMint.

steps.title: Set the record to EXECUTING
steps.detail: SetStateToExecuting flips the conversion record before the burn.

steps.title: Create the source-chain burn operation
steps.detail: CreateBridgingBurnOperation asks blockchain for the burn, with this workflow as OnCompleteSignaledWorkflowID.

steps.title: Check the burn operation exists
steps.detail: CheckOperationExists, gated by version marker BridgingOperation_CheckBurnOperationExists.

steps.title: Await, verify and poll the burn to a final state
steps.detail: WaitOnChainOperationFinalState with verification step BURN.

branches.when: burn result is not EXECUTED (ISSUER_REJECTED or ON_CHAIN_FAILED)
branches.then: IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup and return that result. Nothing was minted, so this is the safe failure

steps.title: Create the destination-chain mint operation
steps.detail: CreateBridgingMintOperation asks blockchain for the mint on the destination chain, again signalling this workflow on completion.

steps.title: Check the mint operation exists
steps.detail: CheckOperationExists for the mint, gated by version marker BridgingOperation_CheckMintOperationExists.

branches.then: NotifyFailingBridgingMint runs on a disconnected context before the error propagates

steps.title: Await, verify and poll the mint to a final state
steps.detail: WaitOnChainOperationFinalState with verification step MINT, including the rpc-lib validation of the minted supply.

branches.then: NotifyFailingBridgingMint on a disconnected context, then the cancellation propagates
NotifyFailingBridgingMint, then IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup, then return that result

steps.title: Alert on a burn without a mint
steps.detail: NotifyFailingBridgingMint is the burn-without-mint alarm. The source-chain burn has already landed, so the customer's tokens are gone with nothing issued on the destination chain: the worst state this workflow can reach. It is raised from three places (mint-operation check cancelled, mint wait cancelled, mint not EXECUTED) and the cancellation paths run it on a disconnected context so the alert survives cancellation.

steps.title: Return EXECUTED
steps.detail: Both legs confirmed on their respective chains.

steps.title: Cleanup on cancellation
steps.detail: handleIssueRedeemWorkflowCancellation runs IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion on a disconnected context.

outcomes.meaning: Burn confirmed on the source chain and mint confirmed on the destination chain.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to roll back.

outcomes.meaning: An endorser rejected either leg.
outcomes.rollback: If it happened on the burn leg, cleanup released holds and nothing moved. If it happened on the mint leg, the burn stays landed and NotifyFailingBridgingMint has fired: manual issuance is required.

outcomes.meaning: Either leg reached a failed final state on chain.
outcomes.rollback: Same asymmetry as above: a failed mint leaves an irreversible burn behind and only an alert.

outcomes.meaning: Cancellation reached the workflow.
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion. If the burn had landed, NotifyFailingBridgingMint fires on a disconnected context; the burn itself is not reversed.

failureHandling: Cleanup runs on a disconnected context via HandleWorkflowCancellation, so it still completes after the workflow context has been cancelled.

RunChildWorkflow returns a *CanceledError raw instead of wrapping it, so a cancelled child routes the parent to CANCELED rather than FAILED. The four permitted termination outcomes are tabulated in .claude/skills/workflow-termination/SKILL.md.
NotifyFailingBridgingMint is fire-and-forget: its own error is discarded so the alert attempt can never mask the underlying failure.

workflows.name: SwappingOperation

trigger.detail: Child of IssueRedeemConversionRequestExecution when OperationType is SWAP (cross-issuer swap with reserve rebalancing).

workflows.summary: The longest workflow in the queue: burn one issuer's stablecoin, rebalance the reserves that back it, then mint the other issuer's stablecoin. The reserve phase runs per allocation and can fall back to ops moving the reserves by hand.

steps.title: Set the record to EXECUTING
steps.detail: SetStateToExecuting flips the conversion record before the burn.

steps.title: Create the swap burn operation
steps.detail: CreateSwappingBurnOperation, with this workflow as OnCompleteSignaledWorkflowID.

steps.title: Check the burn operation exists
steps.detail: CheckOperationExists, gated by version marker SwappingOperation_CheckBurnOperationExists.

steps.title: Await, verify and poll the burn
steps.detail: WaitOnChainOperationFinalState with verification step BURN.

branches.then: NotifyFailingSwappingBurn (only at version 1 of SwappingOperation_NotifySwapBurnFailure; version 2 logs instead), then IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup, then return that result

steps.title: Prepare the reserve allocations
steps.detail: PrepareSwapReserveAllocations works out which burn wallet, mint wallet, asset and amount each reserve movement needs. Version marker SwappingOperation_PerAllocActivity selects this per-allocation path.

branches.then: skip the automatic phase entirely and go to the manual fallback (step 11)

steps.title: Initiate one allocation's reserve transfer
steps.detail: For each allocation, InitiateSingleSwapReserveTransfer creates the custody withdraw/deposit transfer (a short create-only activity; in production the endorsement is signed with Cloud KMS) and returns its operation ID.

branches.then: flag the allocation for manual transfer
retry the initiate with the attempt counter incremented
go to the manual fallback

steps.title: Poll that transfer from inside the workflow
steps.detail: pollSingleReserveTransfer loops on CheckSingleSwapReserveTransfer (single attempt, 2-minute StartToClose) with durable workflow.Sleep at a 10-second recheck interval, so the wait survives worker restarts. Version marker SwappingOperation_PollReserveInWorkflow chose this over the legacy in-activity poll.

branches.when: custody is down: CheckSingleSwapReserveTransfer returns CustodyErr as a value, or the activity itself errors
branches.then: exponential backoff from a 5-second base capped at 30 seconds; once the error streak has run continuously for 15 minutes, NotifyReserveTransferCheckError fires once. The streak and its one-shot flag reset as soon as custody responds again
NotifyReserveTransferNeedsApproval fires once per allocation, then polling continues
re-run the whole initiate-and-poll cycle for this allocation with a new attempt number
NotifyFailedReserveTransfer (version marker SwappingOperation_PolledNotifyFailure) and route the allocation to the manual fallback

branches.when: the workflow is cancelled during Sleep
branches.then: error returns and the cancellation cascade runs

steps.title: Confirm the settled transfer
steps.detail: ConfirmSingleSwapReserveTransfer persists the reserve movement so reconciliation and the mint phase can see it. Version marker SwappingOperation_PolledConfirmTransfer; the legacy in-activity poll did this inline.

steps.title: Reconcile the automatic reserve movements
steps.detail: CreateSwapReserveMovementsRecon runs only when every allocation settled automatically.

steps.title: Legacy single-shot reserve transfer (replay path)
steps.detail: Runs instead of steps 5 to 9 for executions started before SwappingOperation_PerAllocActivity: CreateSwappingReservesTransfer does the transfer and its polling inside one long activity.

branches.then: retry the activity with an incremented attempt (version marker SwappingOperation_RetryEndorsementsOnRejection)
NotifyFailedReserveTransfer, cleanup, result RESERVE_TRANSFER_FAILED
manual fallback

steps.title: Park the swap for manual reserve movement
steps.detail: SetStateToWaitingForManualIntervention moves the record to WAITING_FOR_MANUAL_INTERVENTION so ops can see the swap is theirs. Version marker handleSwapManualTransfer_SetStateToWaitingForManualIntervention.

steps.title: Wait for ops to supply the movement IDs
steps.detail: Awaits SWAP_RESERVE_MANUAL_TRANSFER. Ops move the reserves by hand and send withdraw plus deposit custody operation ID pairs through the SetSwapManualReserveMovements RPC from Retool. There is no timeout on this wait.

branches.when: the channel closes without a signal
branches.then: workflow.ErrCanceled and the cancellation cascade

steps.title: Store the manual movement IDs
steps.detail: SetManualReserveMovementIDs validates and persists the operation ID pairs from the signal.

branches.when: the error is of type ManualTransferValidation
branches.then: ResetManualTransferState, then loop back to step 12 and wait for a corrected set of IDs
propagate; cleanup runs through runWithSwapTechErrorCleanup

steps.title: Reconcile the manual movements
steps.detail: CreateManualSwapReserveMovementsRecon writes the reconciliation for the hand-moved reserves.

branches.when: the error is of type ManualTransferValidation
branches.then: ResetManualTransferState and loop back to step 12; the same retry-friendly loop as step 13

steps.title: Resume execution after the manual transfer
steps.detail: SetStateToExecutingAfterManualTransfer takes the record out of the manual-intervention state. Version marker handleSwapManualTransfer_SetStateToExecutingAfterManualTransfer.

steps.title: Create the swap mint operation
steps.detail: CreateSwappingMintOperation with an attempt counter, followed by CheckOperationExists (version marker SwappingOperation_CheckMintOperationExists).

steps.title: Await, verify and poll the mint, retrying rejections
steps.detail: WaitOnChainOperationFinalState with verification step MINT.

branches.when: result is ISSUER_REJECTED and version marker SwappingOperation_RetryEndorsementsOnRejection is at least 1
branches.then: loop back to step 16 and create a fresh mint operation with the next attempt number, indefinitely
handleMintWaitError fires NotifyFailingSwappingMint on a disconnected context (only for runs before SwappingOperation_RemoveNotifyFailingSwappingMint)
NotifyFailingSwappingMint or an error log, then IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup, then return that result

steps.title: Return EXECUTED
steps.detail: Burn confirmed, reserves rebalanced (automatically or by hand) and mint confirmed.

steps.title: Cleanup on cancellation
steps.detail: handleIssueRedeemWorkflowCancellation runs IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion on a disconnected context. A technical error in the reserve phase goes through runWithSwapTechErrorCleanup, which joins the cleanup error to the original one instead of hiding either.

outcomes.meaning: Burn, reserve rebalance and mint all completed.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to roll back.

outcomes.meaning: The reserve rebalance failed as a business outcome rather than a technical error.
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup failed the on-chain operation and released holds, but the swap burn has already landed and is not reversed.

outcomes.meaning: The burn leg was rejected by an endorser (the mint leg retries rejections instead of returning them).
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup ran before any reserve movement; nothing minted.

outcomes.meaning: Either leg reached a failed final state on chain.
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup ran, but a failed mint leaves the burn and any completed reserve movements in place.

outcomes.meaning: Cancellation reached the workflow, including while parked waiting for the manual reserve signal.
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion. Confirmed burns and settled reserve movements stay.

failureHandling: Cleanup runs on a disconnected context via HandleWorkflowCancellation, so it still completes after the workflow context has been cancelled.

RunChildWorkflow returns a *CanceledError raw instead of wrapping it, so a cancelled child routes the parent to CANCELED rather than FAILED. The four permitted termination outcomes are tabulated in .claude/skills/workflow-termination/SKILL.md.

Custody being unavailable is modelled as data, not failure: CheckSingleSwapReserveTransfer reports CustodyErr as a value so the workflow keeps its own backoff and alerting instead of letting Temporal retry the activity.
Both escalation notifications are one-shot per allocation, so a long outage or a long approval wait produces one alert, not a stream.
All Notify* activities are fire-and-forget: their errors are logged and discarded.
workflows.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant W as SwappingOperation
  participant B as Blockchain
  participant C as Custody
  participant T as Retool
  W->>B: CreateSwappingBurnOperation
  B-->>W: signal ON_CHAIN_CONFIRMATION (burn)
  W->>W: PrepareSwapReserveAllocations
  loop per allocation
    W->>C: InitiateSingleSwapReserveTransfer
    W->>C: CheckSingleSwapReserveTransfer (durable Sleep 10s)
    C-->>W: pending / CustodyErr / NeedsApproval / Rejected / done
    W->>C: ConfirmSingleSwapReserveTransfer
  end
  Note over W,C: 15m custody-down streak -> one-shot alert; Rejected -> re-initiate
  opt manual fallback
    W->>W: SetStateToWaitingForManualIntervention
    T->>W: signal SWAP_RESERVE_MANUAL_TRANSFER (op ID pairs)
    W->>W: SetManualReserveMovementIDs (validation error -> reset and re-await)
  end
  W->>B: CreateSwappingMintOperation
  B-->>W: signal ON_CHAIN_CONFIRMATION (mint)
  Note over W,B: ISSUER_REJECTED -> new mint op, retry
  W-->>W: EXECUTED

workflows.name: AuthorizeConversionFromAPI

trigger.detail: Started by the REST v2 handler for POST /stablecoins/conversion immediately after IssueRedeemConversionRequestHandler returns, when the request carried an API-signed endorsement.

workflows.summary: The API-key endorsement path. Instead of a human signing in the dashboard, an API-signed endorsement is applied to the authorization operation created by the request handler.

steps.title: Receive the endorsement payload
steps.detail: Started with AuthorizationOperationID, the APISignedEndorsement, the caller IP, the API user and the user token. The REST handler refuses the request outright when no endorsement is present, so this workflow only ever starts with one.

steps.title: Apply the API endorsement to the authorization operation
steps.detail: AuthorizeAPIConversion calls IssueRedeemService.AuthorizeIssueRedeemConversionFromAPI, which validates the signature, IP and token and endorses the off-chain authorization operation.

branches.then: record a heartbeat, sleep and retry inside the activity; the loop does not give up
an informational log is emitted and the loop keeps going
the loop exits with the context error

steps.title: Endorsement lands on the off-chain operation
steps.detail: Once the authorization operation reaches a signing decision, blockchain signals OFFCHAIN_VISUAL_APPROVAL_SIGNING_RESULT to {issueRedeemID}-request-execution, which is what actually unblocks execution.

steps.title: Return the authorization operation ID
steps.detail: The REST handler does not block on this workflow's completion; it returns the AuthorizationOperationID from the request handler to the API caller.

steps.title: Cleanup on cancellation
steps.detail: The same handleIssueRedeemWorkflowCancellation deferred handler as the operation workflows: IssueRedeemWorkflowCleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion on a disconnected context.

outcomes.meaning: Cancellation reached the workflow before the endorsement was applied.
outcomes.rollback: Cleanup plus CancelIssueRedeemConversion; no on-chain effect had happened on this path.

failureHandling: Cleanup runs on a disconnected context via HandleWorkflowCancellation, so it still completes after the workflow context has been cancelled.

RunChildWorkflow returns a *CanceledError raw instead of wrapping it, so a cancelled child routes the parent to CANCELED rather than FAILED. The four permitted termination outcomes are tabulated in .claude/skills/workflow-termination/SKILL.md.
The retry loop lives inside the activity rather than in Temporal's retry policy, so the workflow history stays small while the activity heartbeats every attempt.

workflows.name: AssetConfigChangeApproval

trigger.detail: gRPC MintBurn.RegisterStablecoinConfiguration writes a PENDING StablecoinAssetConfigChangeRequest row and then starts this workflow.

workflows.summary: Puts a stablecoin's configuration change (minter/burner roles, contract addresses, limits) behind issuer-org quorum. Approval persists the new configuration together with the endorsements that authorized it.

steps.title: Create the config-approval signing operation
steps.detail: CreateAssetConfigApprovalSigning asks blockchain for the off-chain visual-approval operation. OnSignSignaledWorkflowID is this workflow's own execution ID (it is its own signal target, unlike the conversion handler which targets its child), and the idempotency key is workflowID + "-" + runID. The operation is created with DelayCompletion so it stays parked in signing.

steps.title: Wait for the quorum decision
steps.detail: Awaits ASSET_CONFIG_APPROVAL_SIGNING_RESULT. No workflow-level timeout.

branches.when: the channel closes without a signal
branches.then: workflow.ErrCanceled; the deferred handler flips the change request to REJECTED

steps.title: Resolve the change request
steps.detail: ResolveAssetConfigApproval reads the resolved operation and decides the outcome. The VisualSignPayload is deterministic JSON hashed with SHA256 at signing time and rebuilt and byte-compared on verification, so a payload that differs by a single byte from what quorum signed cannot be accepted. Verification is gated by flag release-mintburn-verify-asset-config-endorsements.

branches.then: the pending configuration and its endorsements are persisted into the live stablecoin_assets_configuration table; request state APPROVED
the change request is flipped to REJECTED and the live configuration is untouched

branches.when: the rebuilt payload does not match the signed bytes
branches.then: verification fails and the change is not applied

steps.title: Release the parked approval operation, only on approval
steps.detail: Signals blockchainworkflows.ChannelDelayCompletion for the authorization operation. A rejected operation is already in a terminal failed state, so nothing is signalled on that path.

steps.title: Return the asset type and operation IDs
steps.detail: Returns AssetTypeID and AuthorizationOperationID.

steps.title: Reject the pending change on cancellation or failure
steps.detail: handleAssetConfigChangeApprovalCancellation routes through HandleWorkflowCancellation and runs RejectAssetConfigChange, so a cancelled approval never leaves a change request stuck in PENDING.

outcomes.meaning: Issuer-org quorum signed the change; the new configuration and its endorsements are live.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is rolled back. Reverting a configuration means submitting a new change request.

outcomes.meaning: Quorum declined, the signed payload failed verification, or the workflow was cancelled.
outcomes.rollback: The live configuration was never touched; the change request row ends REJECTED.

failureHandling: Cleanup runs on a disconnected context via HandleWorkflowCancellation: RejectAssetConfigChange still lands after the workflow context has been cancelled.

RunChildWorkflow returns a *CanceledError raw instead of wrapping it, so a cancelled child routes the parent to CANCELED rather than FAILED. The four permitted termination outcomes are tabulated in .claude/skills/workflow-termination/SKILL.md.

The workflow ID is keyed on the asset type alone, so ALLOW_DUPLICATE is what lets a later change request for the same asset start a fresh run once the previous one closed. A start is still rejected while a run with that ID is open, which keeps at most one approval in flight per asset -- REJECT_DUPLICATE would have blocked every subsequent change for that asset forever.

workflows.name: CoinductorPolicyEndorsementRequestHandler

trigger.detail: gRPC CreateAutomationPolicy (issuer/customer creates a MINT or BURN Coinductor automation policy; also reachable from GraphQL mutation createCoinductorAutomationPolicy)

workflows.summary: Front door for creating a Coinductor automation policy. It starts the endorsement-execution child BEFORE creating the quorum endorsement operation, so a signing result can never arrive before the child that awaits it. Policy entity CoinductorAutomationPolicy moves through PENDING, ACTIVE, PAUSED, REVOKE_PENDING, DISABLED (only DISABLED is terminal); this workflow leaves the policy in PENDING and hands the decision to the child.

steps.title: Accept CreateAutomationPolicy
steps.detail: The gRPC call CreateAutomationPolicy starts this handler. The automation policy row is persisted in coinductor_automation_policies in state PENDING: it exists and is visible to operators, but no deposit event will act on it until it is endorsed and activated.

steps.title: Start the endorsement-execution child first
steps.detail: The child CoinductorPolicyEndorsementExecution is started BEFORE the endorsement operation exists. This ordering is deliberate: if the operation were created first, quorum could endorse it and the POLICY_ENDORSEMENT_SIGNING_RESULT signal could be delivered before the child workflow existed to receive it, and the signal would be lost. Child-first closes that race.

steps.title: CreatePolicyEndorsementOperation
steps.detail: Creates the off-chain endorsement operation that customer quorum must sign to activate the policy. The signing result is delivered back to the child started in step 2. Once the operation exists, the handler's job is done; the outcome is decided entirely by the child.

outcomes.meaning: Policy row written in PENDING, child started, endorsement operation created. Activation or rejection is the child's outcome, not this workflow's.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo on the happy path; the policy is not yet acting on any event while PENDING.

failureHandling: Cancellation is handled by the shared HandleWorkflowCancellation path on a disconnected context, so cleanup work can still run after cancel.

Because the child is started before the endorsement operation is created, a failure between the two leaves a started child waiting on a signal that will never arrive; the 15-day timer in the child is what eventually resolves that case.
versionMarkers: No workflow-specific GetVersion marker recorded in the research brief; mintburn carries 15+ markers repo-wide.

workflows.name: CoinductorPolicyEndorsementExecution

trigger.detail: Started by CoinductorPolicyEndorsementRequestHandler before the endorsement operation is created

workflows.timeout: 15 days for the endorsement decision (in-workflow timer, not a Temporal run timeout)
workflows.summary: Waits for customer quorum to endorse a new Coinductor automation policy and applies the decision. Policy entity CoinductorAutomationPolicy moves through PENDING, ACTIVE, PAUSED, REVOKE_PENDING, DISABLED (only DISABLED is terminal): endorsement takes PENDING to ACTIVE, rejection or a 15-day timeout takes it to DISABLED, and cancellation deliberately leaves it PENDING.

steps.title: AwaitPolicyOperationID by polling storage
steps.detail: The child does not learn the endorsement operation id from a signal. It polls its own storage until the parent's CreatePolicyEndorsementOperation has written the id. The reason is trust: a signal carrying the operation id would be spoofable by anything that can signal the workflow, whereas storage is written only by the parent's activity.

steps.title: Select over signing result, 15-day timer, or cancellation
steps.detail: A Temporal selector waits on three things at once: the POLICY_ENDORSEMENT_SIGNING_RESULT signal, a 15-day timer, and the workflow context being cancelled. Whichever fires first decides the branch.

branches.then: continue to CheckPolicyEndorsementResult
DisablePolicy: the policy is never activated
no cleanup; the policy is left in PENDING for an operator (see the failure step)

steps.title: CheckPolicyEndorsementResult
steps.detail: Reads the actual endorsement outcome rather than trusting the signal payload, then routes on it.

branches.then: ActivatePolicy
DisablePolicy

branches.when: result is non-terminal (neither endorsed nor rejected)
branches.then: hard error: the workflow fails rather than guessing, so the situation is visible instead of silently resolved

steps.title: ActivatePolicy
steps.detail: Moves the policy from PENDING to ACTIVE. From this point deposit events matching the policy can trigger CoinductorAutomationWorkflow runs.

steps.title: DisablePolicy
steps.detail: Terminal state for a rejected endorsement or a 15-day timeout: the policy becomes DISABLED and can never fire. DISABLED is the only terminal policy state.

steps.title: Cancellation leaves the policy PENDING on purpose
steps.detail: On cancellation this workflow runs no cleanup and does not disable the policy. The policy stays PENDING so an operator can see and resolve it, rather than the system quietly disabling something a customer had asked for. This is one of the four permitted termination outcomes documented in .claude/skills/workflow-termination/SKILL.md.

outcomes.meaning: Quorum endorsed the policy; ActivatePolicy moved it to ACTIVE and it can now trigger automation runs.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo; the policy is later stopped through the revoke workflows, not by rolling this back.

outcomes.meaning: Quorum rejected the endorsement; DisablePolicy moved the policy to DISABLED.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing was executed, so nothing is undone; the policy row remains for audit in DISABLED.

outcomes.meaning: No decision within 15 days; DisablePolicy moved the policy to DISABLED.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo. The customer must create a new policy.

outcomes.meaning: Cancelled before a decision. The policy is intentionally left PENDING.
outcomes.rollback: No cleanup is performed; the PENDING policy is the operator's to resolve.

failureHandling: A non-terminal endorsement result is a hard error, not a silent skip, so the case surfaces instead of resolving itself arbitrarily.
The 15-day timer guarantees no policy sits PENDING forever waiting on quorum.
Cancellation runs on a disconnected context via HandleWorkflowCancellation, and by design performs no cleanup here.
versionMarkers: No workflow-specific GetVersion marker recorded in the research brief; mintburn carries 15+ markers repo-wide.

workflows.name: CoinductorPolicyRevokeRequestHandler

trigger.detail: gRPC DisablePolicy (also reachable from GraphQL mutation revokeCoinductorAutomationPolicy)

workflows.summary: Front door for revoking an existing Coinductor automation policy. It parks the policy in REVOKE_PENDING while remembering the state it came from, then starts the revoke-execution child and creates the quorum endorsement operation. Policy entity CoinductorAutomationPolicy moves through PENDING, ACTIVE, PAUSED, REVOKE_PENDING, DISABLED (only DISABLED is terminal). It uses ALLOW_DUPLICATE rather than REJECT_DUPLICATE: the workflow id is derived from the policy, and a revoke can legitimately be requested again after an earlier revoke attempt ended (rejected or reverted), so the same id must be reusable. The brief records the choice as deliberate and justified; the justification comment itself lives in code, not in the brief.

steps.title: InitiateRevokePolicy
steps.detail: Moves the policy to REVOKE_PENDING and records PreRevokeStatus, the state the policy held before the revoke was requested (typically ACTIVE or PAUSED). PreRevokeStatus is what makes a failed revoke reversible instead of destructive.

steps.title: Start the revoke-execution child
steps.detail: Starts CoinductorPolicyRevokeExecution, which will await the revoke signing result. As with the endorsement path, the child is started before the endorsement operation is created so the signing result cannot outrun its receiver.

steps.title: CreatePolicyRevokeEndorsementOperation
steps.detail: Creates the off-chain endorsement operation that quorum must sign to confirm the revoke. Revoking automation is itself a quorum-gated action, not a unilateral one.

outcomes.meaning: Policy is in REVOKE_PENDING with PreRevokeStatus recorded, the child is running, and the revoke endorsement operation exists.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is undone here; if quorum rejects or the wait times out, the child calls RevertRevoke to restore PreRevokeStatus.

failureHandling: ALLOW_DUPLICATE means a repeat DisablePolicy call for the same policy starts a new run instead of being rejected.
PreRevokeStatus is captured before anything else changes, so the revoke is always reversible.
Cancellation goes through HandleWorkflowCancellation on a disconnected context.
versionMarkers: No workflow-specific GetVersion marker recorded in the research brief; mintburn carries 15+ markers repo-wide.

workflows.name: CoinductorPolicyRevokeExecution

trigger.detail: Started by CoinductorPolicyRevokeRequestHandler before the revoke endorsement operation is created

workflows.summary: Waits for quorum to endorse the revoke of a Coinductor automation policy and applies the decision. Policy entity CoinductorAutomationPolicy moves through PENDING, ACTIVE, PAUSED, REVOKE_PENDING, DISABLED (only DISABLED is terminal): an endorsed revoke lands on DISABLED, while a rejected or timed-out revoke calls RevertRevoke to put the policy back to its PreRevokeStatus so it never gets stranded in REVOKE_PENDING.

steps.title: Await the revoke signing result
steps.detail: Blocks on the POLICY_REVOKE_SIGNING_RESULT signal delivered when quorum acts on the revoke endorsement operation created by the parent.

branches.then: check the revoke endorsement result
RevertRevoke to PreRevokeStatus

steps.title: Check the revoke endorsement result
steps.detail: Reads the recorded endorsement outcome and routes on it, rather than trusting the signal payload.

branches.then: DisablePolicy
RevertRevoke to PreRevokeStatus

steps.title: DisablePolicy
steps.detail: The revoke was endorsed: the policy becomes DISABLED, the only terminal policy state, and will never trigger another automation run.

steps.title: RevertRevoke to PreRevokeStatus
steps.detail: The revoke was rejected or timed out: the policy is restored to the PreRevokeStatus recorded by the request handler (for example back to ACTIVE), so a failed revoke attempt is not allowed to leave automation half-off in REVOKE_PENDING.

outcomes.meaning: Revoke endorsed; the policy is DISABLED permanently.
outcomes.rollback: Not reversible: DISABLED is terminal, and a new policy must be created to automate again.

outcomes.meaning: Quorum rejected the revoke; the policy is restored to PreRevokeStatus and keeps running.
outcomes.rollback: REVOKE_PENDING is undone by RevertRevoke; nothing else was changed.

outcomes.meaning: No revoke decision in time; the policy is restored to PreRevokeStatus.
outcomes.rollback: REVOKE_PENDING is undone by RevertRevoke.

failureHandling: Both rejection and timeout converge on RevertRevoke, so REVOKE_PENDING is never a resting state.
Cancellation goes through HandleWorkflowCancellation on a disconnected context; RunChildWorkflow surfaces *CanceledError raw to the parent.
versionMarkers: No workflow-specific GetVersion marker recorded in the research brief; mintburn carries 15+ markers repo-wide.

workflows.name: CoinductorAutomationWorkflow

trigger.detail: Pub/Sub. MintEventSubscriber on coinductor-fiat-deposit-completed-sub consumes custody FiatDepositCompletedEvent and calls HandleMintTrigger (MINT); BurnEventSubscriber on coinductor-deposit-attribution-hold-change-sub consumes DepositAttributionHoldChangeEvent and calls HandleBurnTrigger (BURN). Gated by LaunchDarkly flag release-coinductor-automation-run-trigger.

workflows.summary: The automated mint/burn path. A deposit event from custody is matched against an ACTIVE Coinductor automation policy, passes six validation gates, and if it survives them mintburn records an automation run, opens an issue/redeem conversion, and runs the normal IssueOperation or RedeemOperation child. Optionally it then creates an automated withdrawal to the policy's trusted destination and has stablecoins-autopen endorse it on the customer's behalf. Registered on the ISSUE_REDEEM worker (not the COINDUCTOR worker) because it dispatches the same issue/redeem children as the customer-initiated path.

steps.title: Deposit event arrives
steps.detail: MINT is driven by custody's FiatDepositCompletedEvent (fiat landed, so mint against it). BURN is driven by DepositAttributionHoldChangeEvent (stablecoin deposit attributed and held, so burn it and pay fiat out). mintburn fails to boot if either subscription is missing, so a silently missing subscription cannot degrade into no automation.

steps.title: HandleMintTrigger / HandleBurnTrigger match the event to a policy
steps.detail: The subscriber handler looks up the Coinductor automation policy the event should act on. Everything from here to step 9 runs in the subscriber path, before any Temporal workflow exists, so a rejection at this stage is an ACK-and-skip rather than a failed workflow.

steps.title: Gate 1 of 6: amount is positive
steps.detail: The triggering amount must be positive. All six gates are soft-fails by design: they are the routine 'this event is not for us' cases, not errors.

branches.then: ACK the Pub/Sub message and skip: no run, no conversion, no workflow. Nothing is retried, because a redelivery would fail the same gate.

steps.title: Gate 2 of 6: policy type matches the trigger
steps.detail: A MINT policy may only be triggered by the mint event source and a BURN policy only by the burn event source. Policy types are MINT and BURN.

branches.when: policy type does not match the trigger
branches.then: ACK the Pub/Sub message and skip

steps.title: Gate 3 of 6: organization matches the policy
steps.detail: The event's organization must be the organization the policy was endorsed for. This is what stops one customer's policy from acting on another customer's deposit.

branches.when: org does not match the policy
branches.then: ACK the Pub/Sub message and skip

steps.title: Gate 4 of 6: vault matches the policy
steps.detail: The event's vault must be the vault named in the policy, so quorum's endorsement is scoped to the exact account the automation may move value in and out of.

branches.when: vault does not match the policy
branches.then: ACK the Pub/Sub message and skip

steps.title: Gate 5 of 6 (MINT only): source organization is not the issuer
steps.detail: For MINT, the deposit's source organization must not be the issuer organization. Issuer-originated movements are not customer deposits, and treating them as such would mint against the issuer's own funds.

branches.when: MINT and the source org is the issuer
branches.then: ACK the Pub/Sub message and skip

steps.title: Gate 6 of 6 (BURN only): asset matches the policy
steps.detail: For BURN, the deposited asset must be the stablecoin the policy covers, so a deposit of some other token cannot be burned under this policy.

branches.when: BURN and the asset does not match the policy
branches.then: ACK the Pub/Sub message and skip

steps.title: dispatchAutomationRun: record the run and the conversion
steps.detail: All six gates passed. A row is written to coinductor_automation_runs in state PROCESSING and an issue/redeem conversion record is created, so the automated attempt is durable and auditable before any workflow starts.

steps.title: Start {issueRedeemID}-coinductor-automation
steps.detail: The workflow id is derived from the issue/redeem id, and an AlreadyStarted error is swallowed. That makes Pub/Sub redelivery safe: a duplicate event for the same conversion joins the existing run instead of starting a second mint or burn.

branches.then: swallowed: the existing run continues, the duplicate delivery is ACKed

steps.title: Dispatch the issue/redeem child by type
steps.detail: MINT dispatches IssueOperation, BURN dispatches RedeemOperation, both on the ISSUE_REDEEM queue. The automated path reuses the same state machines and the same on-chain execution as customer-initiated conversions; only the authorization route differs.

branches.then: child IssueOperation (fiat in, mint on chain)
child RedeemOperation (burn on chain, fiat out)

steps.title: HoldCustomerFunds
steps.detail: Places the hold in custody on the customer funds the conversion will consume, before the child executes anything, so the balance cannot be spent twice.

steps.title: RunChildWorkflow and inspect the result
steps.detail: Runs the child through the shared RunChildWorkflow wrapper (which returns *CanceledError raw so cancellation propagates honestly) and branches on the result.

branches.then: continue to the automated withdrawal tail

branches.when: child returns anything other than EXECUTED
branches.then: CoinductorWorkflowCleanup (release holds) then SetCoinductorAutomationRunFailed; the run is FAILED

steps.title: MaybeCreateAutomatedWithdrawal
steps.detail: Optional tail. If the policy names a trusted destination, mintburn creates the withdrawal that moves the newly minted stablecoin (or the fiat proceeds of the burn) out to it. Coinductor withdrawals carry an amlproto structured submission for travel-rule reporting. 'Maybe' is literal: a policy without a destination finishes here.

branches.when: the policy has no automated withdrawal destination
branches.then: skip the tail and finalize the run as COMPLETED

steps.title: AutoEndorseAutomatedWithdrawal
steps.detail: The withdrawal operation is created in a state that waits for INITIATOR_REQUIRED, and stablecoins-autopen (the autopengateway CVM, reached over mTLS on :8099) endorses it on the customer's behalf so no human has to sign each automated withdrawal. This is the step that makes the end-to-end journey unattended.

steps.title: Poll CheckAutomatedWithdrawal with exponential backoff
steps.detail: The workflow polls the withdrawal's status with exponential backoff and durable sleeps rather than holding a long activity open, because an automated withdrawal can sit in risk review for days. Polling in the workflow keeps that wait replay-safe.

branches.then: finalize the run as COMPLETED
run FAILED with reason AUTOMATED_WITHDRAWAL_FAILED

steps.title: finalizeAutomationRun
steps.detail: Writes the terminal run state. A run reaches COMPLETED only once the automated withdrawal has actually settled; a completed mint or burn with a pending withdrawal is still PROCESSING.

steps.title: A failed withdrawal does not unwind the mint or burn
steps.detail: When the tail fails, the run is FAILED with reason AUTOMATED_WITHDRAWAL_FAILED, but the mint or burn has already been executed and confirmed on chain and is NOT rolled back. The value stays where the child left it (minted into the customer's vault, or burned with the fiat leg already done) and the undelivered withdrawal is an operator follow-up. Read a FAILED run as 'the automated delivery did not happen', never as 'nothing happened'.

outcomes.meaning: The mint or burn executed AND, where the policy asked for one, the automated withdrawal settled. COMPLETED is only reached once the withdrawal is done.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo.

outcomes.meaning: The issue/redeem child returned something other than EXECUTED. CoinductorWorkflowCleanup released the holds and SetCoinductorAutomationRunFailed recorded the run as FAILED.
outcomes.rollback: Holds taken by this run are released. Anything the child itself declined to unwind (for example a burn that already landed on chain) stays as the child left it.

outcomes.meaning: The mint or burn succeeded but the automated withdrawal did not settle; the run is FAILED with this reason.
outcomes.rollback: The committed mint or burn is NOT rolled back. No on-chain reversal, no re-mint, no re-burn is attempted; only the withdrawal needs operator follow-up.

outcomes.meaning: One of the six validation gates rejected the event. The Pub/Sub message is ACKed and no conversion, workflow or on-chain action is created.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo: the gates run before any state is written.

failureHandling: All six validation gates soft-fail: the message is ACKed and the run is skipped, so a non-matching event is not retried forever.
AlreadyStarted on workflow start is swallowed, making Pub/Sub redelivery idempotent for a given issue/redeem id.
Non-EXECUTED child results go through CoinductorWorkflowCleanup plus SetCoinductorAutomationRunFailed rather than leaving the run in PROCESSING.
The withdrawal tail polls with exponential backoff in the workflow because risk review can take days.
A failed automated withdrawal never triggers a compensating mint or burn; it is reported, not reversed.
Cancellation is handled by HandleWorkflowCancellation on a disconnected context; RunChildWorkflow returns *CanceledError raw.

workflows.name: TokenizationOperation

trigger.detail: gRPC MintTokenization / BurnTokenization, REST POST /v2/tokenization/mint and /v2/tokenization/burn (via readonlyapi), GraphQL mutation tokenize

workflows.timeout: 30 minutes for the on-chain final-state poll
workflows.summary: Single-leg tokenization for tokenized_deposit assets: one on-chain mint or burn with no fiat leg and no paired conversion. autoEndorse is true, so mintburn endorses the operation itself through EndorseOperationFromAPI and no human quorum is involved.

steps.title: CreateOnChainOperation
steps.detail: Creates the on-chain mint or burn operation for the tokenized_deposit asset and records it in tokenization_operations_history with status PENDING.

steps.title: CheckOperationExists
steps.detail: Confirms the operation is really there before anything waits on it, so the workflow never blocks on an operation that was never created.

steps.title: EndorseOperationFromAPI (autoEndorse = true)
steps.detail: Tokenized deposits are endorsed automatically by mintburn rather than by an operator quorum. This is the single step that separates this workflow from the gold variant.

steps.title: Await on-chain confirmation
steps.detail: Blocks on the TOKENIZATION_ON_CHAIN_CONFIRMATION signal, delivered when the operation reaches a chain state worth acting on.

steps.title: PollOnChainOperationFinalState (30m)
steps.detail: Does not trust the signal as the final word: polls the operation's real final state for up to 30 minutes to establish success or failure.

branches.when: operation reached a successful final state
branches.then: UpdateOperationStatus to SUCCESS

branches.when: operation failed on chain or the poll does not resolve
branches.then: failCustodyOperationAndRecordOutcome, status ERROR

steps.title: UpdateOperationStatus
steps.detail: Writes the terminal tokenization status, SUCCESS or ERROR, to the tokenization operation record.

steps.title: failCustodyOperationAndRecordOutcome
steps.detail: Every failure path funnels here: the custody operation is failed and the outcome recorded, so a tokenization record is never left sitting in PENDING. An unresolved PENDING record would be indistinguishable from work still in flight, which is exactly what this avoids.

outcomes.meaning: The single on-chain tokenization leg confirmed and the record is SUCCESS.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo.

outcomes.meaning: The operation failed on chain, or the 30-minute final-state poll did not establish success. failCustodyOperationAndRecordOutcome ran.
outcomes.rollback: The custody operation is failed and the outcome recorded. There is no compensating on-chain transaction: nothing was minted or burned on a failure, so there is nothing to reverse.

failureHandling: All failure paths run failCustodyOperationAndRecordOutcome, so no record stays PENDING.
CheckOperationExists prevents awaiting a confirmation for an operation that does not exist.
PollOnChainOperationFinalState is the authority on the outcome, not the signal.
Cancellation is handled by HandleWorkflowCancellation on a disconnected context.

trigger.detail: gRPC MintTokenization / BurnTokenization, REST POST /v2/tokenization/mint and /v2/tokenization/burn (via readonlyapi), GraphQL mutation tokenize, for tokenized_gold assets

workflows.summary: The tokenized_gold variant of tokenization. Same single-leg shape as TokenizationOperation, with two deliberate differences: autoEndorse is false, so a manual operator quorum must endorse the operation, and only one gold operation per asset may be in flight at a time.

steps.detail: Only a single gold tokenization operation may be in flight for a given asset. Concurrent gold mints or burns on the same asset are not allowed, which keeps supply changes serialised against the physical backing.

branches.when: another gold operation for the same asset is already in flight
branches.then: the new operation is not admitted

steps.title: CreateOnChainOperation
steps.detail: Creates the on-chain gold mint or burn operation and records it in tokenization_operations_history with status PENDING.

steps.title: CheckOperationExists

steps.title: Manual quorum endorsement (autoEndorse = false)
steps.detail: EndorseOperationFromAPI is deliberately NOT called for gold. The operation sits waiting for a human operator quorum to endorse it outside this workflow; the workflow only moves on when the on-chain confirmation for the endorsed operation arrives.

steps.title: PollOnChainOperationFinalState (30m)
steps.detail: Polls the operation's real final state for up to 30 minutes rather than trusting the signal payload.

branches.when: operation reached a successful final state
branches.then: UpdateOperationStatus to SUCCESS

branches.when: operation failed on chain or the poll does not resolve
branches.then: failCustodyOperationAndRecordOutcome, status ERROR

steps.title: failCustodyOperationAndRecordOutcome
steps.detail: Every failure path fails the custody operation and records the outcome, so no gold tokenization record is left PENDING and the in-flight slot for that asset is not held open indefinitely.

outcomes.meaning: The quorum-endorsed gold leg confirmed on chain and the record is SUCCESS.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo.

outcomes.meaning: The gold operation failed on chain, or the 30-minute final-state poll did not establish success. failCustodyOperationAndRecordOutcome ran.
outcomes.rollback: The custody operation is failed and the outcome recorded; no compensating on-chain transaction is issued because nothing was minted or burned.

One in-flight gold operation per asset removes concurrent-supply-change races.
All failure paths run failCustodyOperationAndRecordOutcome, so no record stays PENDING.

workflows.name: ManualDepositApprovalWorkflow

trigger.detail: gRPC CreateManualDeposit (ops-recorded fiat deposit: FEDWIRE, SWIFT, CHIPS or BOOK). In production the approver organization is pinned by configuration.

workflows.summary: Records a fiat deposit that ops observed out of band and pushes it to the bank once an operator quorum approves. The deposit is PROPOSED, an off-chain approval operation gathers the quorum signature, and only an APPROVED deposit is submitted to bankadapter and marked CREDITED.

steps.title: CreateManualDepositOffChainApproval
steps.detail: Writes the manual deposit as PROPOSED in manual_deposits_history and creates the off-chain approval operation that operator quorum must endorse. This operation is NOT a child workflow of this one, which is the root of the known gap gap-mintburn-manual-deposit-orphan-op.

steps.title: Await the endorsement signing result
steps.detail: Blocks on the MANUAL_DEPOSIT_ENDORSEMENT_SIGNING_RESULT signal, delivered when operator quorum acts on the off-chain approval operation.

steps.title: IsManualDepositOffChainEndorsed
steps.detail: Reads the recorded endorsement state rather than trusting the signal payload, and routes on it.

branches.then: the deposit becomes APPROVED and continues to the bank submission
the deferred handler marks the deposit REJECTED; nothing is sent to the bank

steps.title: Signal ChannelDelayCompletion
steps.detail: Signals ChannelDelayCompletion once the deposit is APPROVED, releasing whatever was waiting on the approval decision before the bank leg runs.

steps.title: SubmitManualDepositToBank
steps.detail: Submits the approved deposit to bankadapter using a deterministic id, so a Temporal retry of this activity cannot create a second bank-side deposit for the same record.

steps.title: Mark the deposit CREDITED
steps.detail: Terminal happy path: the deposit is recorded as CREDITED once bankadapter has accepted it.

steps.title: Deferred handler marks REJECTED unless approved
steps.detail: A deferred handler ensures that any exit without an approval marks the deposit REJECTED, so a PROPOSED deposit does not linger as if still under review. The known limitation is on the other side: because the off-chain approval operation is not a child workflow, it is not cancelled or cleaned up with this workflow and can stay stuck awaiting a signature that will never be applied. See gap-mintburn-manual-deposit-orphan-op.

outcomes.meaning: Operator quorum approved the deposit and bankadapter accepted the submission.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is undone by this workflow; a credited deposit is corrected through the bank and accounting, not by rerunning this workflow.

outcomes.meaning: Quorum did not endorse, or the workflow exited without an approval; the deferred handler marked the deposit REJECTED.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing was submitted to the bank, so there is nothing to reverse. The off-chain approval operation may remain open (gap-mintburn-manual-deposit-orphan-op).

failureHandling: The deferred handler marks the deposit REJECTED on any exit that is not an approval, so PROPOSED is not a resting state.
SubmitManualDepositToBank uses a deterministic id, making the bank submission idempotent under Temporal retries.
Known gap: the off-chain approval operation is not a child workflow and can stay stuck; tracked as gap-mintburn-manual-deposit-orphan-op.
Cancellation is handled by HandleWorkflowCancellation on a disconnected context.

workflows.name: FetchReservesComposition

trigger.detail: Temporal Schedule reserves-composition-fetch, running at 17:00, 20:00 and 23:00 UTC. mintburn's only cron.

workflows.summary: Ingests reserve-attestation data from BigQuery three times a day and stores one snapshot per stablecoin per report date. This is a read-and-record pipeline with no quorum: it moves no value, so nothing needs endorsing. It backs the public reserves API and raises a Slack alert when the reserve ratio looks anomalous.

steps.title: GetCursors
steps.detail: Reads the ingestion cursors so the run only pulls data it has not already stored, instead of re-reading the full history on every schedule fire.

steps.title: FetchReservesData
steps.detail: Queries the reserve reconciliation tables in BigQuery (anc-global-analytics.stablecoin_issuance.<coin>_stablecoin_recon) for the covered stablecoins: USDGO, USDtb, USDPT, fUSD and ZLUSD.

steps.title: StoreReservesSnapshot per row
steps.detail: Writes one row of reserves_composition_history per returned row, keyed idempotently on {Stablecoin}|{ReportDate} so the three daily runs and any retry cannot duplicate a snapshot. Each snapshot carries TotalStablecoinOnNetwork, TotalReserves, ReserveRatio, Adjustments and ReserveComponents, plus the dual-verification fields FirstVerifiedBy and SecondVerifiedBy: a snapshot is attested by two distinct verifiers (through VerifyReservesSnapshot) rather than one, so no single person can sign off published reserve figures.

steps.title: Notify on reserve-ratio anomaly
steps.detail: If a snapshot's reserve ratio looks anomalous, the run posts to the Slack webhook wired up for reserve anomalies (STA-1011). The alert is the whole intervention: the run does not block or withhold the snapshot.

branches.then: post a Slack anomaly alert; the snapshot is still stored

steps.title: Snapshot becomes readable
steps.detail: Stored snapshots are served through GetReservesHistory and VerifyReservesSnapshot on gRPC, REST GET /v2/stablecoins/reserves (via readonlyapi) and the GraphQL reservesHistory query, all behind the release-mintburn-reserves-rest-api and release-mintburn-reserves-entitled-rest-api flags.

outcomes.meaning: Snapshots for the fetched rows are stored under their {Stablecoin}|{ReportDate} keys, and any anomaly was alerted to Slack.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo: the workflow only records data. A wrong snapshot is corrected by a later run for the same key or by the dual-verification review, not by a rollback.

failureHandling: The {Stablecoin}|{ReportDate} idempotency key makes retries and the three daily runs safe: the same report date cannot be stored twice.
Cursors mean a failed run is recovered by the next scheduled fire without re-reading everything.
No quorum gate exists on this path because it moves no value; dual verification (FirstVerifiedBy / SecondVerifiedBy) is applied after storage, not before.
Cancellation is handled by HandleWorkflowCancellation on a disconnected context.

workflows.name: EndorseExecuteOperation (mint / burn auto-endorsement)

trigger.detail: mintburn calls the gRPC EndorseExecuteOperation on the CVM VIP :8099 after polling custody until the execute operation reaches SIGS_REQUIRED. This is a synchronous request handler, not a Temporal workflow.

workflows.summary: The live path that lets a stablecoin mint or burn proceed without a human quorum: the gateway re-fetches the operation, resolves the asset, runs the ordered policy chain under a global lock with an audit-row reservation, signs a CertEndorsementPayload with its attested certificate, and submits it to custody, where the HSM checks the same decision again.

steps.title: Resolve the execute operation id
steps.detail: The issue/redeem workflow reads the custody execute operation id off the IssueRedeemConversion record it owns.

steps.title: Poll custody until SIGS_REQUIRED
steps.detail: mintburn polls every 5s for at most 60 attempts, because the gateway can only add an endorsement while the operation is waiting for signatures.

branches.when: the operation has already moved past SIGS_REQUIRED
branches.then: mintburn records AlreadyEndorsed and does not call the gateway
mintburn stops; the endorsement does not happen, result FAILED_UPSTREAM

steps.title: Call EndorseExecuteOperation over mTLS
steps.detail: EndorseExecuteOperation{operation_id} is sent over mTLS to the CVM VIP on :8099 (10.50.88.2 dev, 10.100.248.2 staging, 10.150.124.2 production). A feature-flagged router decides between the legacy in-cluster address and the CVM.

branches.when: the client certificate OU is not `mintburn`
branches.then: the mTLS listener refuses the connection; mintburn sees Unauthenticated or PermissionDenied and classifies it as Errored (it pages)

steps.title: Fetch the execute operation and resolve the asset
steps.detail: The gateway calls custody GetExecuteOperation for the operation and its VisualSigningParams, then resolves the asset and token type from asset_type_id through assetregistry. A degraded assetregistry response still carries the organization so an alert can be routed. The token-type check is fail-closed.

branches.when: the asset shape is not an allowed token type (isAllowedTokenType / token-type policy, fail-closed)
branches.then: deny: audit row DEFERRED, result DENIED

branches.when: assetregistry answers in a degraded mode
branches.then: the request still names the organization so the notification is routable

steps.title: Take the global endorsement lock and reserve an audit row
steps.detail: A global endorsement lock serialises decisions, then the decision is taken and a row is written to autopen_endorsements_audit before any signature exists, then the transaction commits and the lock is released. Reserving before signing is what makes the rolling 24h cap safe.

branches.then: the row is written DEFERRED and does not count toward the rolling cap

branches.when: the CVM crashes after the PROCESSING row is committed
branches.then: the row stays PROCESSING and keeps counting toward the rolling cap, which is conservative by design

steps.title: Run the ordered policy chain
steps.detail: Always-on stages run first: op-classification, amount-resolver, irc-augmentation, asset-config-augmentation, mintburn-cross-check, coinductor-run-augmentation, coinductor-cross-check. Then the gates named in ANCHOR_POLICY_ADAPTERS run: organization-allowlist, per-kind asset allowlist, per-kind max amount and rolling-window-cap. The first non-nil error denies and short-circuits signing. Stage names may change with the 2026-08-20 redesign (gap-autopen-policy-chain-redesign).

branches.when: the operation amount cannot be resolved from the operation and its parameters
branches.then: deny: audit row DEFERRED, result DENIED

branches.when: no issue/redeem conversion (IRC) exists for the operation, or the IRC does not match it
branches.then: deny: audit row DEFERRED, result DENIED

branches.when: the mintburn asset configuration does not match the operation's asset or parameters
branches.then: deny: audit row DEFERRED, result DENIED

branches.when: the organization is not in ANCHOR_ALLOWED_ORGANIZATION_IDS (organization-allowlist, configured in staging and production)
branches.then: deny: audit row DEFERRED, result DENIED

branches.when: the asset is not in ANCHOR_ASSET_ALLOWLIST_<KIND> for this operation kind
branches.then: deny: audit row DEFERRED, result DENIED

branches.when: the amount is at or above ANCHOR_MAX_AMOUNT_<KIND> (production: 1000 mint, 1000 burn, 0 withdrawal)
branches.then: deny: audit row DEFERRED, result DENIED

branches.when: the rolling 24h mint plus burn total would exceed ANCHOR_ROLLING_WINDOW_CAP_AMOUNT (production 10000, dev and staging 100000000)
branches.then: deny: audit row DEFERRED, result DENIED
deny-all: nothing can be endorsed. An empty ANCHOR_POLICY_ADAPTERS value is refused at startup rather than silently allowing everything

steps.title: Build and sign the endorsement payload
steps.detail: From the same snapshot the chain evaluated, the gateway takes the EndorsedParamsDigest (custody GetOperation), builds CertEndorsementPayload{OperationID, APPROVE, EndorsedParamsDigest}, signs its canonical form with the attested Ed25519 key and attaches the DER certificate chain.

branches.when: the leaf certificate has under 7h of validity left
branches.then: ErrCertNearExpiry: no signature is produced. Rotation at about 40h keeps this from happening in steady state (40h + 7h <= 48h)

steps.title: Submit EndorseOperationWithCert; the HSM re-validates
steps.detail: custody accepts the endorsement on the strength of the certificate-embedded signature (the call carries no caller-identity auth, README Open Risk 6) and the HSM checks the decision a second time.

branches.when: the HSM finds the organization missing from its own allowlist, the decision not APPROVE, or the endorsedParamsDigest not bound to the operation
branches.then: the HSM refuses and the endorsement fails even though the gateway chain allowed it; the two allowlists must be kept in sync

steps.title: Finalize the audit row
steps.detail: finalizeEndorsement runs on a detached context with a 30s budget so the row is closed out even if the request context is already gone.

branches.then: the row stays PROCESSING and continues to count toward the rolling cap

steps.title: Notify exactly once per outcome
steps.detail: NotificationService raises exactly one incident.io alert per endorsement outcome through the shared alert source, routed by the env attribute.

branches.then: a note is attached to that operation's alert so the endorsement and the conversion line up

outcomes.meaning: The chain allowed it, the HSM accepted the certificate endorsement and custody recorded it; the mint or burn can proceed to signing.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is undone. The endorsement is a signed artifact on the custody operation; stopping the operation afterwards is a custody-side action, not a gateway one.

outcomes.meaning: A policy stage returned an error. The audit row is DEFERRED and does not count toward the rolling cap.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing was signed, so there is nothing to undo. The custody operation stays in SIGS_REQUIRED and needs a human quorum endorsement instead.

outcomes.meaning: The gateway answered with a non-transport error (it has already raised its own incident.io alert). mintburn only warns.
outcomes.rollback: No endorsement exists; the operation waits for humans.

outcomes.meaning: A transport-class error (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Canceled, Unauthenticated, PermissionDenied). mintburn treats this as its own problem and pages.
outcomes.rollback: Unknown whether the gateway got as far as a PROCESSING row; that row, if written, keeps counting toward the cap until finalized.

outcomes.meaning: The operation had already moved past SIGS_REQUIRED when mintburn polled, so no call was made.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing happened.

failureHandling: mintburn splits gateway errors: transport errors (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Canceled, Unauthenticated, PermissionDenied) become Errored and page; everything else becomes FailedUpstream and only warns, because the gateway has already alerted.
The signer fails closed: with CVM_BOOTSTRAP_MODE set there is no PEM fallback, so a missing or stale credential means no endorsements rather than unattested ones.
A crash between reserving and finalizing leaves a PROCESSING row that keeps consuming rolling-cap headroom until it is reconciled.
