workflows.name: Automated withdrawal endorsement

trigger.detail: Reached from the tail of a Coinductor automation run in mintburn: MaybeCreateAutomatedWithdrawal creates the custody withdraw operation and then asks the gateway to endorse it. Built and exercised in development and staging; denied in production.

workflows.summary: The same endorsement machinery applied to execute.Withdraw operations that a Coinductor automation run created, with two extra chain stages that tie the withdrawal back to a real run. In production the withdrawal allowlist is empty and the ceiling is 0, so every one of these is denied on purpose.

steps.title: Coinductor run completes
steps.detail: An automation run finishes its mint or burn leg and reaches the point where the customer's automated withdrawal should be created.

steps.title: MaybeCreateAutomatedWithdrawal creates the custody operation
steps.detail: mintburn creates a custody withdraw operation with initiator AutopenInitiator_V1. It is idempotent through the run's WithdrawalOperationID, so a retried run reuses the same operation instead of creating a second withdrawal.

branches.when: the run already has a WithdrawalOperationID
branches.then: the existing operation is reused; no duplicate withdrawal is created

steps.title: Ask the gateway to endorse the withdrawal
steps.detail: The coinductor CoinductorWithdrawalService call site invokes EndorseExecuteOperation on the CVM over mTLS, the same RPC the mint/burn path uses.

steps.title: coinductor-run-augmentation loads the run
steps.detail: The gateway fetches the Coinductor run behind the withdrawal from mintburn's :9095 mTLS listener.

branches.when: no Coinductor run backs the operation
branches.then: deny: an automated withdrawal with no run is never endorsed

steps.title: coinductor-cross-check compares run and operation
steps.detail: The run's status, organization, amount, asset and destination must all agree with the custody withdraw operation.

branches.when: run status, organization, amount, asset or destination disagrees with the operation
branches.then: deny: audit row DEFERRED, result DENIED

steps.title: Withdrawal gates: allowlist and ceiling
steps.detail: The per-kind allowlist and per-kind max amount are read for the WITHDRAWAL kind: ANCHOR_ASSET_ALLOWLIST_WITHDRAWAL and ANCHOR_MAX_AMOUNT_WITHDRAWAL.

branches.when: production, where ANCHOR_ASSET_ALLOWLIST_WITHDRAWAL is empty and ANCHOR_MAX_AMOUNT_WITHDRAWAL is 0
branches.then: every automated withdrawal is denied. This is deliberate and stays that way pending STA-1195 / STA-1196 (gap-autopen-withdrawals-denied-prod)

branches.when: development or staging, where the withdrawal allowlist carries the test assets and the ceiling is 10000000
branches.then: the withdrawal can be endorsed and the flow continues into the shared sign-and-submit path

steps.title: Shared sign, submit and finalize path
steps.detail: From here the flow is identical to the mint/burn endorsement: reserve the audit row, sign CertEndorsementPayload, submit EndorseOperationWithCert to custody, let the HSM re-validate, finalize the row and raise one incident.io alert.

outcomes.meaning: Development and staging only today: the withdrawal carries an automated endorsement and can be signed.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is undone by the gateway.

outcomes.meaning: The run is missing, the cross-check disagreed, or the withdrawal gates rejected it. In production this is the outcome for every automated withdrawal.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing was signed. The withdraw operation remains and needs the normal human endorsement path.

failureHandling: Idempotency lives in mintburn: the run's WithdrawalOperationID prevents a retry from creating a second withdraw operation.
A denial is recorded DEFERRED and does not consume rolling-cap headroom, so the production deny-all costs nothing operationally.
versionMarkers: Production enablement is tracked by STA-1195 and STA-1196.

workflows.name: CVM boot, attestation and certificate rotation

trigger.detail: The CVM's init script runs on every boot, and again roughly every 40h when the process takes a jittered SIGTERM for certificate rotation.

workflows.summary: How the CVM earns the right to sign: it generates a fresh key, proves to the HSM which measured image is asking, receives a 48h certificate chain, and hands both to the service on stdin. Rotation is the same loop running again about every 40 hours.

steps.title: init script sets the per-project environment
steps.detail: init-stablecoins-autopen.sh reads the project id from the metadata server and branches on it to set the service project, policy adapters, asset allowlists, ceilings, OTLP endpoint, secret paths and DB settings for that environment.

branches.when: the project id is not one of the three Ironclave projects
branches.then: the script errors out rather than booting with a default configuration

steps.title: Run see-runner
steps.detail: see-runner performs the attestation exchange inside the CVM and is the only producer of the signing credential.

steps.title: Generate an ephemeral Ed25519 key and a CSR
steps.detail: The key never leaves the CVM. The CSR uses CN stablecoins-autopen.anchorage.internal, and a nonce is computed over the CSR so the attestation is bound to this exact key.

steps.title: Produce a TDX quote and the CCEL log
steps.detail: The Intel TDX quote plus the CCEL event log describe the measured UKI that is running, with the CSR nonce inside, so the HSM can tell which image is asking for which key.

branches.then: a mocked quote is used; this is refused in production

steps.title: Request boot-measurement approval over IAP
steps.detail: A staff token for cvm-address-provider@anchorage.internal is used to call the risk GraphQL API through IAP and raise an "approve boot measurements" operation against HSM_CVM_ORG_KEY_ID.

steps.title: Poll for approval
steps.detail: The script polls the operation up to 150 times at 2s intervals waiting for the HSM to approve the measurements.

branches.when: boot approval fails or never arrives
branches.then: the script sleeps 30s and retries the whole attestation; the VM stays unhealthy and the load balancer sends it no traffic

steps.title: Receive the HSM-signed payload and set credentials
steps.detail: The HSM returns a signed payload; set_credentials turns it into a 48h leaf certificate chain over the in-CVM public key.

steps.title: Spawn the service with the payload on stdin
steps.detail: /stablecoins-autopen is started with JSON {signingPrivateKey, certificateChain} on stdin. CVM_BOOTSTRAP_MODE selects CVMSigner, which accepts nothing else: there is no PEM fallback in deployed environments, so the signer fails closed.

branches.when: the payload is absent or unusable
branches.then: the signer refuses to initialise and the service endorses nothing

steps.title: Serve and become healthy
steps.detail: The gRPC server listens on :8099 over mTLS and the health server on :8098; once the MIG health check passes, the internal load balancer starts routing mintburn's traffic to this instance.

steps.title: Rotate at about 40 hours
steps.detail: cert_rotation.go raises a jittered SIGTERM at roughly 40h, which returns control to the init loop for a fresh attestation and a fresh 48h certificate. The invariant is 40h + the 7h sign-time floor <= the 48h leaf lifetime, so a signing request never meets an expired certificate.

branches.when: signing is attempted with under 7h of certificate validity left
branches.then: ErrCertNearExpiry: the request is refused rather than signed with a nearly expired certificate
the CVM stops deliberately; this is the intended way to take an instance down

outcomes.meaning: The instance holds an HSM-issued 48h certificate over an attested in-CVM key and is behind the load balancer.
outcomes.rollback: Not applicable; the previous credential is simply gone.

outcomes.meaning: Boot approval failed, so the script sleeps 30s and re-attests. The instance never becomes healthy and takes no traffic.
outcomes.rollback: No credential was issued.

outcomes.meaning: The process exited 0, which deliberately stops the CVM.
outcomes.rollback: Not applicable.

failureHandling: Fail-closed by construction: no attestation means no certificate, and no certificate means no endorsements rather than unattested ones.
Two replicas per environment mean one instance can be rotating or re-attesting while the other serves.
MIG auto-heal recreates an instance whose :8098 health check keeps failing.
versionMarkers: The running CVM image is set out of band: the MIG instance-template version has ignore_changes and Terraform holds a cos-stable placeholder (gap-autopen-cvm-image-out-of-band).

workflows.name: MintBurnValidation

trigger.detail: Hexagate monitor hit delivered as POST /webhooks/hexagate/primary-market-issuance (alias route POST /webhooks/hexagate) on the public Botón gateway.

workflows.summary: Takes one observed mint or burn on an allowlisted token contract and tries to explain it with Anchorage's own records: the Custody execute operation for the transaction hash, then the mintburn issue/redeem record for that operation id. If either record is missing, or if the on-chain data disagrees with the internal record, it pages incident.io.

steps.title: Hexagate posts the monitor hit
steps.detail: A Hexagate monitor configured by hand in the Hexagate UI observes a function call on a watched contract and posts the payload to the primary-market route. Typical payload is around 1100 bytes. Because the monitor set lives outside the repo, the repo cannot tell you which contracts are actually being watched (gap-boton-hexagate-monitors-manual).

steps.title: HTTP handler gates the request
steps.detail: The handler applies a chain of cheap rejections before any Temporal work is started: body is capped at 16 KiB with http.MaxBytesReader; the RSA-PSS X-Hexagate-Signature is verified; the payload is parsed. Everything that is a well-formed request but not interesting is swallowed with a 200 so Hexagate does not retry it.

branches.then: request is truncated and rejected
401, no workflow started
400, no workflow started

branches.when: the call is neither a mint nor a burn
branches.then: 200 and drop; nothing to reconcile

branches.when: the token contract is not on the environment's allowlist
branches.then: 200 and drop

branches.when: a workflow for this TxHash is already running
branches.then: 200; REJECT_DUPLICATE on the workflow id makes the duplicate a no-op

steps.title: Start MintBurnValidation
steps.detail: Workflow id is mint-burn-validation-<TxHash> with REJECT_DUPLICATE reuse, so the transaction hash is the deduplication key across the whole system. Execution timeout is 25h, one hour more than the polling schedule below needs.

steps.title: GetOperationByTxHash — poll Custody for the execute operation
steps.detail: Calls Custody GetExecuteOperationForTxReceiptID for the transaction hash. Retry is driven by the workflow, not by an activity retry policy, so the wait survives worker restarts: up to 13 attempts with the backoff schedule 0s, 1m, 3m, 7m, 15m, 31m, 1h3m, 2h7m, 4h15m, 8h31m, and then capped at 5h for the remaining attempts, about 24h of total coverage. The long tail exists because an on-chain transaction can be seen by Hexagate before Anchorage's own record of it has settled.

branches.then: one single OperationNotFoundRetrying early-warning alert is sent, so a human learns about the mismatch within a quarter of an hour instead of a day; no further early-warning alerts are sent for this workflow

branches.when: the operation is found on any attempt
branches.then: polling stops and the workflow continues to the issue/redeem lookup
OperationNotFound alert; result Valid=false; the workflow ends without reaching validation

steps.title: GetIssueRedeemRecord — find the matching issue/redeem record
steps.detail: Calls mintburn GetIssueRedeemHistory with page size 100 over a 7-day lookback, heartbeating to Temporal while it pages so a long scan is not mistaken for a hung activity. A record matches if the Custody operation id equals ANY ONE of the record's operation-id fields: IssuerOperationId OR IssuerConversionOperationId, plus IssuerFundingOperationId for a burn. The OR match is what lets a single on-chain event be explained by whichever leg of the issue/redeem flow actually created the operation.

branches.when: no record in the 7-day window matches on any operation-id field
branches.then: IssueRedeemNotFound alert; result Valid=false
the record is carried into ValidateOnChainData

steps.title: ValidateOnChainData — three checks
steps.detail: Compares the on-chain call against the internal record and accumulates a list of Discrepancies rather than failing on the first one, so one alert can carry everything that is wrong.

branches.then: an issue must appear on chain as a mint and a redeem as a burn; bridge and swap operations may legitimately produce either. A mismatch is a ValidationMismatch discrepancy.

the on-chain counterparty is compared with Custody GetWalletAddress for the expected wallet; on Solana the associated token account is derived rather than compared directly. A mismatch is a ValidationMismatch discrepancy.

amounts are compared after whole-token truncation with a plus or minus 1 tolerance, which absorbs decimal-precision differences between the chain and the internal record. A mismatch is a ValidationMismatch discrepancy.

steps.title: AlertOnDiscrepancy — page incident.io
steps.detail: If any discrepancy accumulated, one incident.io alert is raised with dedupe key boton-mintburn-<chain>-<contract>. The key is deliberately per contract, not per transaction: a contract that has started producing unexplainable mints pages once and then stays quiet until that alert is resolved, instead of paging on every transaction. Alert types are OperationNotFound, OperationNotFoundRetrying, IssueRedeemNotFound and ValidationMismatch. incident.io is configured only in staging and production.

steps.title: Loud failure on infrastructure or alert-send errors
steps.detail: A validation failure is a normal, expected outcome and is reported through incident.io. An infrastructure error, or a failure to send the alert itself, fails the workflow loudly instead of being swallowed, because a Botón that cannot page is a monitor that is silently off.

outcomes.meaning: Both internal records were found and all three checks passed. Result Valid=true and the workflow is silent: no alert, no page.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo; Botón only observes on this path.

outcomes.meaning: Result Valid=false with at least one discrepancy: OperationNotFound, IssueRedeemNotFound or ValidationMismatch. An incident.io alert has been raised under the per-contract dedupe key.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is undone. Botón does not stop, reverse or block the on-chain operation on the primary-market path; the alert is the only action, and remediation is human.

outcomes.meaning: An infrastructure error or a failed alert send. The workflow fails loudly and Temporal retains the history.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is undone; the validation verdict for that transaction is unknown until someone re-runs or investigates.

failureHandling: Custody lookup misses are expected and handled by the 13-attempt, roughly 24h workflow-driven backoff rather than by activity retries, so the wait outlives worker restarts and deploys.
The attempt-5 early-warning alert is sent exactly once, so a slow-settling record does not produce a paging storm while it settles.
GetIssueRedeemRecord heartbeats while paging through history so Temporal does not time it out as hung.
ValidateOnChainData accumulates discrepancies instead of returning on the first one, so one alert reports every problem found.
Alert-send failures fail the workflow rather than being logged and dropped.

workflows.name: SecondaryMarketBridgeEvaluationWorkflow

trigger.detail: Hexagate monitor hit on a LayerZero bridge contract, delivered as POST /webhooks/hexagate/secondary-market-issuance. Hexagate does not resend on a 500, so the handler returns 2xx as soon as the workflow has been started and all real work happens inside Temporal.

workflows.summary: Classifies one LayerZero bridge event against the Role x Impact response matrix and acts on the verdict: it pages the bridging on-call and, for the highest-impact rows, calls Pause on bridgingauthorizer to stop the bridge without waiting for a human.

steps.title: Hexagate posts the bridge event
steps.detail: A Hexagate monitor on a LayerZero contract posts to the secondary-market route. Because Hexagate does not resend on a 500, a Botón error after the response is sent means the event is simply lost, which is why the handler starts the workflow and returns 2xx before doing anything expensive.

steps.title: Handler verifies the signature and starts the workflow
steps.detail: Same signature verification as the primary-market route, then StartSecondaryMarketBridgeEvaluationWorkflow with workflow id bridge-event-evaluation-<txHash>-<eventID>, keyed on transaction hash plus event id so two events in the same transaction each get their own workflow. Execution timeout 1h.

steps.title: EvaluateBridgeEvent — parse the event details
steps.detail: First part of the pure classification activity. Hexagate describes what it saw in prose, so the event name is recovered from one of two shapes: "emitted an event Foo" yields the event Foo, and "Function foo was called" yields the synthetic name fc:foo. Function calls and emitted events therefore share one namespace in the matrix.

branches.when: the details string matches neither shape
branches.then: unparseable: InputError, counted under boton.bridge.events with catalog_case unparseable

steps.title: Registry lookup — resolve the contract
steps.detail: The event's address and chain are looked up in the BridgeContractRegistry built by lzconfig.Load(env), which yields the contract's role (SendUln302, ReceiveUln302, EndpointV2, OFTAdapter, ProxyAdmin or DVN) and, for token-scoped roles, its dvnType of test-token or production-token. Hexagate's negative chain ids (Hoodi -376, Celo -377, Morph -372) are remapped through hexagateChainIDOverrides before the lookup.

branches.when: the address is not in the registry
branches.then: unknown_contract: InputError, counted under boton.bridge.events with catalog_case unknown_contract. This is a drift detector: it usually means a Hexagate monitor was pointed at a contract that lzconfig does not know about.

steps.title: Matrix lookup — classify (contract, event)
steps.detail: The (contract role, event name) pair is looked up in the classify.go response matrix, producing the verdict: monitoring-plan catalog case, tier T0 or T1, blast radius, shouldPage and shouldPause.

branches.when: no matrix row exists for the pair
branches.then: unmapped: InputError, counted under boton.bridge.events with catalog_case unmapped. Also a drift detector: a monitored contract has started emitting something the matrix has no opinion about.

steps.title: Refine hook
steps.detail: A per-case refinement step adjusts the verdict where the event name alone is not enough. It is used for the DVN RoleGranted and RoleRevoked events, where which role was touched decides how bad the event is.

steps.title: Test-token gating
steps.detail: If the event belongs to a test-token deployment, the pause leg is suppressed and the tier is downgraded from T0 to T1. The reason is that the authorizer's pause is GLOBAL: there is one kill switch for the bridge, not one per token, so pausing on a test-token event would freeze production lanes. Test-token admin wallets are also lower-assurance and cannot themselves mint or move real value. Gating suppresses only the pause, never the page: the page always fires, and there is no override for the tier downgrade. For chain-wide contracts the owning OApp is attributed by decoding the event arguments; if attribution fails, the code is fail-conservative and keeps the matrix verdict rather than assuming test-token.

branches.when: the contract is a test-token deployment, or a chain-wide event is attributed to one
branches.then: pause suppressed, tier downgraded T0 to T1, page unchanged

branches.when: OApp attribution of a chain-wide event fails
branches.then: the matrix verdict stands, including any pause

steps.title: Pause override, then log and count
steps.detail: ANCHOR_OVERRIDE_PAUSE_BRIDGE_ENABLED and ANCHOR_OVERRIDE_PAUSE_BRIDGE_VALUE (both default false) can replace the pause verdict for an incident, for example to stop Botón pausing repeatedly while an issue is being worked. The override never suppresses the page. The final verdict is logged and counted under boton.bridge.events with its catalog_case, and PauseOverridden records that the override was in play.

branches.then: its value replaces shouldPause; shouldPage is untouched

steps.title: Rejected input is non-retryable
steps.detail: unparseable, unknown_contract and unmapped are all returned as InputError and marked non-retryable, because retrying will not make a payload parse or a matrix row appear. Any other error is retried within the activity's ScheduleToCloseTimeout. The three drift counters on boton.bridge.events are how these rejections become visible instead of silent.

steps.title: Dispatch PageBridgeEvent and PauseAuthorizer CONCURRENTLY
steps.detail: The workflow starts both legs before waiting on either: PageBridgeEvent is executed if shouldPage and PauseAuthorizer if shouldPause, and their futures are collected before any Get. The two run CONCURRENTLY, so containment is not queued behind the page and a slow incident.io call cannot delay the pause.

branches.when: shouldPage and shouldPause are both true (for example an EndpointV2 InboundNonceSkipped, PacketBurnt or fc:clear event)
branches.then: both activities are dispatched at once

branches.when: shouldPage only (for example a rate-limit config change, or any test-token-gated event)
branches.then: only the page is dispatched; the authorizer has its own pre-sign rate check

branches.when: neither (the three count-only DVN rows: VerifySignaturesFailed, HashAlreadyUsed, ExecuteFailed)
branches.then: LogWarn plus the counter only; nobody is woken up

steps.title: PageBridgeEvent — raise the page
steps.detail: Raises the incident.io alert with dedupe key boton-bridge-<chain>-<contract>-<tx>-<event>-<eventID>, lowercased. Unlike the per-contract key on the primary-market path, this key is per event occurrence, so every distinct bridge event gets its own page. Tier T0 routes to the bridging on-call and T1 to a broader audience; both page today.

steps.title: PauseAuthorizer — pull the bridge kill switch
steps.detail: Calls bridgingauthorizer Pause with the alert title as the reason, so whoever later reads GetPauseState sees why the bridge stopped. Pause is idempotent, so a repeat call during an incident is harmless. The pause is global to the bridge, which is exactly why test-token events are gated out of this leg.

steps.title: Join semantics — pause failure never fails the workflow, page failure does
steps.detail: Both futures are then awaited. A PauseAuthorizer failure is recorded and swallowed: it NEVER fails the workflow, because the page is the human backstop and a workflow that failed on the pause would put the page's success in doubt. A PageBridgeEvent failure DOES fail the workflow, because an unpaged event is an event nobody knows about, and the Temporal failure is then the last remaining signal.

branches.then: error logged, workflow still succeeds; humans have been paged and can pause manually
the workflow fails; the failed workflow itself is the residual signal

outcomes.meaning: shouldPage was true and shouldPause false: the on-call was paged and the bridge keeps running. Covers rate-limit config changes, the reversible EndpointV2 PacketNilified row, the DVN should-never-fire canaries (RoleAdminChanged, Paused, Unpaused), and any event whose pause was suppressed by test-token gating or by the override.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing on chain is undone; the bridge was never stopped.

outcomes.meaning: shouldPage and shouldPause were both true: the on-call was paged and bridgingauthorizer was paused, concurrently. Covers the unconditional auto-pause rows, EndpointV2 InboundNonceSkipped, PacketBurnt and fc:clear.
outcomes.rollback: The pause is not undone by this workflow. Unpause is a separate bridgingauthorizer RPC with no monorepo caller, so lifting the pause is a deliberate human act outside Botón.

outcomes.meaning: The count-only rows: DVN VerifySignaturesFailed, HashAlreadyUsed and ExecuteFailed. The event is logged at warning level and counted under boton.bridge.events; nobody is paged and nothing is paused.
outcomes.rollback: No action taken.

outcomes.meaning: unparseable, unknown_contract or unmapped. Non-retryable InputError; the event is counted under its drift catalog_case and the workflow ends without paging or pausing. Hexagate will not resend, so these counters are the only way the miss becomes visible.
outcomes.rollback: No action taken; the event is effectively unhandled until someone notices the drift counter.

failureHandling: The handler returns 2xx as soon as the workflow starts, because Hexagate does not resend on a 500.
Classification errors that retrying cannot fix (unparseable, unknown_contract, unmapped) are non-retryable InputErrors; everything else retries within the activity's ScheduleToCloseTimeout.
Page and pause are dispatched concurrently, so neither leg is delayed by the other.
A pause failure never fails the workflow: the page is the human backstop. A page failure does fail it, so the missed page leaves a trace.
Pause is idempotent, so repeated calls during one incident are safe.
Test-token gating is fail-conservative: if OApp attribution of a chain-wide event fails, the matrix verdict stands rather than being downgraded.

sequenceDiagram
  participant HG as Hexagate
  participant B as Boton
  participant T as Temporal
  participant IO as incident.io
  participant BA as bridgingauthorizer
  HG->>B: POST /webhooks/hexagate/secondary-market-issuance
  B->>B: verify signature
  B->>T: start bridge-event-evaluation-txHash-eventID

workflows.name: StablecoinRewardsSavePayouts

trigger.detail: SavePayouts gRPC RPC, called from the Stablecoin Rewards Payouts Retool app (the Generate Payouts step).

workflows.timeout: no workflow timeout; both activities use a 24h StartToClose timeout with WaitForCancellation
workflows.summary: Reads a month of daily per-affiliate yield from BigQuery and aggregates it into one payout row per participant and program, saved as PENDING so staff can review before submitting.

steps.title: Read daily yield rows
steps.detail: ReadRewardData activity queries anc-global-analytics.stables_yield.fct_yield_client_data for the requested StartDate to EndDate range and returns the daily per-affiliate reward rows. In development the fake BigQuery provider serves rows seeded through ConfigureFakeBQClient instead.

steps.title: Aggregate to monthly payouts and insert rows
steps.detail: SaveMonthlyPayouts sums the daily rows per participant and program for the payout month, rounds to the asset precision, verifies every participant is enrolled in the program for the assets they hold (the run fails if not), and inserts payout rows with DefaultStatus PENDING. Intra-org payouts, where the sender and receiver Atlas participant are the same, are written SKIPPED because the operations team settles those by hand. An optional ProgramIDs filter narrows which programs are written.

branches.when: a participant is not enrolled in the program for an asset it holds
branches.then: the activity errors with 'not all participants are enrolled in the programs for the assets they hold' and no payout rows are written

branches.when: sender Atlas participant equals receiver Atlas participant
branches.then: that payout row is written with status SKIPPED instead of PENDING

outcomes.meaning: One PENDING (or SKIPPED) payout row exists per participant and program for the payout date, ready for the Submit Payouts step.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is undone automatically. Rows already inserted stay; a re-run for the same payout date inserts a second set of rows, so staff correct mistakes through UpdatePayout or SQL rather than by re-running.

failureHandling: Both activities inherit a 24h StartToClose timeout and the default retry policy, so a transient BigQuery or DB failure is retried inside the activity rather than failing the workflow.
The enrollment check is a hard stop by design: a missing (participant, program) enrollment would otherwise fail the whole payout run later, which is what the daily reconcile sweep exists to prevent.

workflows.name: StablecoinRewardsEstimatePayouts

trigger.detail: EstimatePayouts gRPC RPC, used to preview a month before generating real payouts.

workflows.timeout: no workflow timeout; activities use a 24h StartToClose timeout
workflows.summary: The same BigQuery read and monthly aggregation as SavePayouts, but the rows are written with status ESTIMATED so they are a preview and are never picked up by the payout fan-out.

steps.title: Read daily yield rows
steps.detail: Reuses the ReadRewardData activity over the same fct_yield_client_data table for the requested date range.

steps.title: Aggregate and insert ESTIMATED rows
steps.detail: EstimateMonthlyPayouts runs the same aggregation with DefaultStatus ESTIMATED. Because MonthlyPayouts only loads PENDING rows for a payout date, estimates cannot be paid out by accident.

outcomes.meaning: Preview payout rows exist for the month with status ESTIMATED.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing is undone; estimate rows are inert and are cleaned up by staff.

failureHandling: Same activity retry behaviour as SavePayouts.

workflows.name: StablecoinRewardsMonthlyPayouts

trigger.detail: Submit Payouts in the Payouts Retool app, via the payMonthlyStablecoinRewards GraphQL mutation (STAFF only), which returns the workflow id.

workflows.timeout: no workflow timeout; activities use a 24h StartToClose timeout
workflows.summary: Loads every PENDING payout for a payout date and starts one SinglePayout child workflow per payout, then waits for all of them.

steps.title: Load the pending payouts for the date
steps.detail: LoadMonthlyPayouts wraps ListPayouts filtered to status PENDING and the requested PayoutDate, and returns only the payout ids. ESTIMATED, SKIPPED, CREATED and COMPLETED rows are therefore never re-paid.

steps.title: Fan out one SinglePayout child per payout
steps.detail: Every payout id becomes a child workflow whose WorkflowID is the payout id itself, with reuse policy ALLOW_DUPLICATE and ParentClosePolicy ABANDON. Using the payout id as the workflow id is what lets the Pub/Sub subscriber signal the right child later without a lookup table, and ABANDON means a child keeps running (and can still be signalled) after the parent closes. All children are started in one loop with no batching, so the fan-out width is the number of pending payouts.

steps.title: Wait for every child
steps.detail: FuturesMultiWait waits on all child futures and joins their errors; the parent fails with 'Failed to execute one or more child workflows' if any child failed, but the successful children have already settled their payouts.

branches.then: the parent returns an error listing them; successful payouts are unaffected

outcomes.meaning: Every pending payout for the month has its own SinglePayout workflow, each of which drives one Settlement Network transfer.
outcomes.rollback: No compensation. Settlements already created stay created; a failed payout returns to PENDING through the settlement-event path and can be retried by a later run.

failureHandling: Children are ABANDONed rather than cancelled, so a parent failure or worker restart does not kill in-flight payouts.
The fan-out is unbounded: unlike the enrollment fan-outs, which were moved to bounded batches after the TMPRL1101 deadlock incident, this loop still starts every child at once.

workflows.name: StablecoinRewardsSinglePayout

trigger.detail: Child of StablecoinRewardsMonthlyPayouts, one per pending payout, with WorkflowID equal to the payout id and ParentClosePolicy ABANDON.

workflows.timeout: none. The code carries an explicit TODO to add a workflow timeout once the manual payout step is removed; activities use a 24h StartToClose timeout with WaitForCancellation.
workflows.summary: Settles one payout: it loads the payout, creates a two-way Settlement Network transfer from the Anchorage sender vault to the participant Atlas participant, then blocks on SETTLEMENT_EVENTS signals until the settlement reaches a final state.

steps.title: LoadPayoutData
steps.detail: Reads the payout row and its participant to get the payout date, participant id, amount and the receiving Atlas participant id. (The activity is registered under the legacy name LoadAtlasParticiantID.)

steps.title: DoSettlementForReward: check the payout is payable
steps.detail: The payout must currently be PENDING; any other status is a hard error naming the actual status. This is the guard that makes the fan-out safe to re-run.

branches.then: hard error 'payout with id X has status Y. expected status is PENDING'; no settlement is created

steps.title: DoSettlementForReward: retry guard and idempotency key
steps.detail: It walks the payout existing settlements. If any of them is CREATED, ACTION_NEEDED or COMPLETED the payout cannot be retried and the activity errors. Otherwise each prior settlement bumps an attempt counter, and the Settlement Network idempotency key becomes <payoutID>-<attempt>, so a genuine retry gets a fresh key while a duplicated call with the same attempt count is deduplicated by Settlement Network.

branches.when: an existing settlement is CREATED, ACTION_NEEDED or COMPLETED
branches.then: hard error 'cannot retry this payout'

steps.title: Resolve the sender participant, vault and per-network wallet
steps.detail: GetSenderAtlasParticipant resolves the Atlas participant for the org in ANCHOR_SENDER_ORG_ID, then GetParticipant on Settlement Network returns its default vault (missing default vault is an error) and its CustomDefaultWallets. The asset network id comes from Asset Registry, and the wallet whose NetworkId matches is chosen (no default wallet for that network is an error). The amount is negated because the sender is paying out.

branches.when: the sender participant has no default vault
branches.then: hard error 'no default vault for participant'

branches.when: no default wallet matches the asset network
branches.then: hard error 'no default wallet found for network <network>'

steps.title: SupportsGasStation for the payout network
steps.detail: custody.SupportsGasStation(networkId, senderOrgKeyId) decides the UseGasStation flag on the settlement, so Anchorage covers the network fee where the gas station supports that chain. An error here propagates and fails the activity.

steps.title: CreateTwoWaySettlement
steps.detail: Proposer is the Anchorage sender Atlas participant, acceptor is the participant Atlas participant, ClientReferenceId is stablecoin-reward-<payoutID> (the memo that lets ops trace a transfer back to a payout), IdempotencyKey is <payoutID>-<attempt>, plus the sender vault, the wallet amount and the gas-station flag.

steps.title: Move the payout to CREATED and record the settlement
steps.detail: The payout status becomes CREATED and a payout_settlements row links the payout id to the returned settlement id. That row is what the Pub/Sub subscriber uses to find the workflow to signal.

steps.title: Await SETTLEMENT_EVENTS until the settlement is final
steps.detail: The workflow loops on the SETTLEMENT_EVENTS channel. Settlement states arriving on it are CREATED and ACTION_NEEDED (not final) and COMPLETED, FAILED, REJECTED and TIMED_OUT (final). Each signal runs UpdatePayoutPostSettlement, which maps the settlement state onto the payout: CREATED to CREATED, COMPLETED to COMPLETED, ACTION_NEEDED to ACTION_NEEDED, and FAILED, REJECTED or TIMED_OUT back to PENDING so the payout can be retried by a later run. The loop breaks on the first final state.

branches.when: the signalled settlement id differs from the one this workflow created
branches.then: hard error 'settlement ID mismatch between returned ID and signaled ID'; the workflow fails rather than mis-attributing a settlement
error 'settlement completion channel closed'

branches.when: the mapped settlement state is final
branches.then: the loop breaks and the workflow completes

steps.title: No workflow timeout
steps.detail: There is no workflow execution timeout, so a payout whose settlement never reaches a final state (for example one parked in ACTION_NEEDED awaiting the manual step) waits indefinitely. The TODO in the code ties removing this to removing the manual payout step. See gap-scr-single-payout-no-timeout.

outcomes.meaning: The settlement executed and the payout is COMPLETED.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing to undo; the transfer is on chain.

outcomes.meaning: The settlement came back FAILED, REJECTED or TIMED_OUT, so the payout was set back to PENDING and the workflow completed.
outcomes.rollback: No money moved. The payout is picked up again by a later MonthlyPayouts run, which creates a new settlement under the next idempotency key <payoutID>-<attempt>.

outcomes.meaning: The workflow failed before or during settlement (payout not PENDING, unretryable existing settlement, missing vault or wallet, custody or Settlement Network error, or a settlement id mismatch).
outcomes.rollback: Whatever the activity already committed stays: if the settlement was created but the follow-up write failed, the payout_settlements row and payout status may lag reality, and the retry guard will then refuse a naive retry until an operator intervenes.

failureHandling: The PENDING precondition plus the CREATED/ACTION_NEEDED/COMPLETED retry guard together make a re-run of MonthlyPayouts safe: an already-settled payout errors instead of double-paying.
The idempotency key <payoutID>-<attempt> gives Settlement Network deduplication for the same attempt and a distinct key for a genuine retry.
The settlement-id equality check turns a mis-routed signal into a hard error rather than a silent status overwrite.
Activities use WaitForCancellation, so a cancelled workflow does not abandon an in-flight settlement call.

workflows.name: Settlement event Pub/Sub subscriber

trigger.detail: settlementnetworkproto.SettlementEvent messages on the Pub/Sub subscription default-settlement-events-stablecoinrewards (topic default-settlement-events).

workflows.summary: Not a Temporal workflow, but modelled as one because it is the only path that advances a payout: it turns each Settlement Network event into a SETTLEMENT_EVENTS signal on the SinglePayout workflow whose id is the payout id.

steps.title: Receive and unmarshal the event
steps.detail: The instrumented subscription hands each message to onMessageReceived, which proto-unmarshals a SettlementEvent.

branches.then: log an error and Nack, so Pub/Sub redelivers

steps.title: Look up the payout by settlement id
steps.detail: GetPayoutIDBySettlementID reads payout_settlements. Most settlements in the environment have nothing to do with rewards, so a miss is normal and cheap.

branches.then: log at info ('ignoring this event') and Ack: the settlement is not a rewards payout
log an error and Nack for redelivery

steps.title: Map the settlement state
steps.detail: STATE_EXECUTED maps to COMPLETED, STATE_ACTION_NEEDED to ACTION_NEEDED, STATE_FAILED to FAILED, STATE_TIMED_OUT to TIMED_OUT and STATE_REJECTED to REJECTED.

branches.when: the state is none of those five
branches.then: log at info that the update is ignored and Ack

steps.title: Signal the payout workflow
steps.detail: SettlementBroadcastChannel.SignalWorkflow targets workflow id payoutID with an empty run id, carrying the settlement id and mapped state. This is why MonthlyPayouts sets the child WorkflowID to the payout id.

branches.then: Ack

branches.when: the error text contains 'workflow execution already completed'
branches.then: log 'Workflow already completed' and Ack, since a late event for a finished payout is not an error
log an error and Nack for redelivery

steps.title: Panic recovery Acks the message
steps.detail: A deferred recover logs 'Panic on Settlement Event subscription ... detected' and Acks, so a poison message cannot loop forever. The trade-off is that a panicking event is dropped rather than retried.

outcomes.meaning: The matching SinglePayout workflow received the settlement state and updated the payout.
outcomes.rollback: n/a

outcomes.meaning: The settlement is not a rewards payout, the state is not one of the five handled ones, or the payout workflow has already completed. The message is Acked.
outcomes.rollback: n/a

outcomes.meaning: Unmarshal, lookup or signal failed in a way that may succeed later; Pub/Sub will redeliver.
outcomes.rollback: n/a

failureHandling: Ack on 'not found' and on unhandled states keeps the subscription from backing up on traffic that is none of its business.
The 'already completed' check is a string match on the error text, with a TODO to check the specific error type instead.

workflows.name: EnrollOrganization

trigger.detail: Self-serve: the enrollOrganizationInStablecoinRewards GraphQL mutation (ORG_USER or STAFF), started as stablecoin-rewards-enroll-organization-<uuid> with REJECT_DUPLICATE. The same workflow also runs as a child of the daily auto-enroll cron, where the parent supplies a deterministic id stablecoin-rewards-enroll-organization-<orgKeyID>-<parentRunID> with reuse policy ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY and ParentClosePolicy REQUEST_CANCEL.

workflows.timeout: no workflow timeout; activities use a 24h StartToClose timeout
workflows.summary: Enrolls one organization: it records terms acceptance and the org enrollment, resolves the org eligible top-level affiliates, and starts an EnrollTopLevelAffiliate child for each one that has no participant yet.

steps.title: AcceptTermsOfService
steps.detail: Records that the acting user accepted the stablecoin rewards self-serve terms for the organization. On the cron path there is no acting user key id.

branches.then: the workflow fails with 'Failed to accept terms of service for organization <org>' and nothing is enrolled

steps.title: MarkOrgAsEnrolled
steps.detail: Writes the org_enrollments row with the requested start date. This row is what makes the org visible to the daily auto-enroll cron and to Organization.isEnrolledInStablecoinRewards.

steps.title: GetTopLevelAffiliateIDsForOrganization with jurisdiction filtering
steps.detail: Walks org to accounts to affiliates to top-level affiliates and, with FilterIneligibleJurisdictions set, drops any affiliate outside the environment approved-jurisdiction list. An org with no eligible affiliate produces the log line 'no top level affiliates found for org <org_id>' that the runbook tells oncall to grep for.

steps.title: Diff against existing participants
steps.detail: GetParticipantIDsByTopLevelAffiliate returns the affiliate-to-participant map, and the workflow keeps only affiliates absent from it. This is what makes the daily re-run cheap and idempotent: already-enrolled affiliates are skipped. One summary log line reports total and pending counts, deliberately instead of a log per affiliate, because this loop runs on the workflow coroutine where per-item logging burns the task yield budget.

steps.title: Fan out EnrollTopLevelAffiliate in batches of 25
steps.detail: Under GetVersion marker bounded-tla-fan-out (v1) the batch size is 25; DefaultVersion keeps the old single-batch shape so histories recorded before the change still replay. Each child gets WorkflowID equal to the top-level affiliate id, ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY and ParentClosePolicy ABANDON. Batches are awaited one at a time; a failing batch does not stop later batches and all errors are joined at the end (errors.Join) so the workflow reports every failure.

branches.when: one or more affiliate children fail
branches.then: the workflow fails with 'Failed to execute one or more child workflows'; affiliates enrolled in other batches stay enrolled

outcomes.meaning: The org has an org_enrollments row and a participant for every eligible top-level affiliate, each enrolled in all approved programs.
outcomes.rollback: None. Terms acceptance and the org_enrollments row survive a later child failure, which is intentional: the daily cron will finish the job.

failureHandling: Every step is idempotent enough to re-run daily: terms acceptance and the org row are upserts, and the affiliate diff skips work already done.
errors.Join across batches means one bad affiliate does not hide the others.
versionMarkers: bounded-tla-fan-out (v1: batches of 25 instead of one unbounded batch)

workflows.name: EnrollTopLevelAffiliate

trigger.detail: Child of EnrollOrganization, one per not-yet-enrolled top-level affiliate, WorkflowID equal to the top-level affiliate id, ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY, ParentClosePolicy ABANDON.

workflows.timeout: no workflow timeout; activities use a 24h StartToClose timeout
workflows.summary: Turns one top-level affiliate into a rewards participant: get or create its Atlas participant, create the participant row, then enroll it in every approved program.

steps.title: GetOrCreateAtlasParticipant
steps.detail: Finds the existing Atlas participant for the top-level affiliate or creates one (CreateParticipant), and makes it a trusted counterparty of the Anchorage sender org so a two-way settlement between them is allowed later.

steps.title: CreateStablecoinRewardsParticipant
steps.detail: Inserts the participants row linking the top-level affiliate, the Atlas participant id and the start date. Participants are 1:1 with top-level affiliates.

steps.title: ListStablecoinRewardsPrograms (Approved)
steps.detail: Lists programs with status Approved; those are the programs a new participant joins.

steps.title: EnrollStablecoinRewardsParticipant in all approved programs
steps.detail: Inserts one enrollment row per (participant, approved program). Programs approved after this run are picked up later by the reconcile sweep, not here.

outcomes.meaning: A participant exists for the affiliate, with an Atlas participant trusted by the sender org, enrolled in every currently approved program.
outcomes.rollback: None. A failure part-way can leave an Atlas participant or a participant row without enrollments; the next daily run and the reconcile sweep converge on the intended state.

failureHandling: ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY on the workflow id means a failed affiliate can be retried by the next run while a successful one is not re-run.
The enrollment insert skips already-enrolled pairs, so re-running is safe.

workflows.name: StablecoinRewardsAutoEnrollOrganizations

trigger.detail: Temporal schedule stablecoin-rewards-auto-enroll-organizations-cron, daily at 16:00 UTC. The schedule is created imperatively by SetSchedule in every worker at startup, not declared in Terraform or Helm.

workflows.timeout: no workflow timeout; activities use a 24h StartToClose timeout
workflows.summary: Daily sweep that re-enrolls every organization already in org_enrollments, so top-level affiliates added since the last run get participants, and then reconciles existing participants into every approved program.

steps.title: Capture the parent run id
steps.detail: Child workflow ids must be derived deterministically from data already in history, so the workflow uses the replay-stable parent RunID instead of a uuid or wall clock. It changes every scheduled run, which keeps child ids unique per run while still letting the same org be re-enrolled daily.

steps.title: ListEnrolledOrganizations
steps.detail: Reads every row of org_enrollments with its start date.

branches.then: the error is captured but the workflow still runs the reconcile child, because a degraded run is exactly when enrollment gaps are most likely

steps.title: Fan out EnrollOrganization in batches of 5
steps.detail: Under GetVersion marker bounded-org-fan-out (v1) at most 5 EnrollOrganization children run concurrently, each batch awaited before the next; DefaultVersion keeps the old single-batch shape for in-flight runs. Child ids are stablecoin-rewards-enroll-organization-<orgKeyID>-<parentRunID>, with ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY and ParentClosePolicy REQUEST_CANCEL. Combined with the 25-affiliate inner batch, this bounds the 16:00 UTC burst that used to grow as orgs x affiliates.

branches.when: one or more org children fail
branches.then: their errors are joined and reported at the end; other orgs are unaffected

steps.title: Run the ReconcileProgramEnrollments child, even after a failure
steps.detail: Under GetVersion marker reconcile-program-enrollments (v1) the workflow always starts child stablecoin-rewards-reconcile-enrollments-<parentRunID> and waits for it, joining its error with any earlier one. Running it after a failed listing or fan-out is deliberate. It exists so a program created after an affiliate was first discovered still picks up the existing participant population.

outcomes.meaning: Every enrolled org has participants for all its current eligible top-level affiliates, and every participant is enrolled in every approved program.
outcomes.rollback: None; the workflow only adds missing rows.

failureHandling: Errors from the listing, the org fan-out and the reconcile child are joined and returned together, so one failure does not hide the others.
Bounded batching (5 orgs, 25 affiliates) was introduced specifically to stop the daily burst from starving workflow goroutines and producing TMPRL1101 potential deadlock task failures.
versionMarkers: reconcile-program-enrollments (v1: always run the reconcile child)

workflows.name: ReconcileProgramEnrollments

trigger.detail: Child of StablecoinRewardsAutoEnrollOrganizations, id stablecoin-rewards-reconcile-enrollments-<parentRunID>, ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY, ParentClosePolicy REQUEST_CANCEL.

workflows.timeout: no workflow timeout; activities use StartToClose 1m and ScheduleToClose 30m with WaitForCancellation
workflows.summary: Enrolls every existing participant into every approved program it is not yet enrolled in, paging through the missing-enrollment diff in batches of 50 with a one-second pause between batches.

steps.title: List approved programs
steps.detail: ListStablecoinRewardsPrograms with status Approved. Programs approved while this workflow runs are picked up by the next daily run.

branches.then: the workflow fails immediately; there is nothing to reconcile against

steps.title: Loop per program, one batch of 50 at a time
steps.detail: For each program: ListParticipantIDsMissingEnrollment with Limit 50, enroll that page, sleep one second, repeat until the diff is empty. Each successful batch removes its participants from the diff, so the loop converges without ever holding the full diff in one activity payload. The one-second pause spaces out a large backfill (for example the first run after a new program) so it trickles into Postgres instead of arriving as a burst of inserts, history-trigger rows and Datastream replication churn. A per-program cap of 10,000 batches bounds history growth if the diff ever stops shrinking.

branches.when: the diff does not converge within 10,000 batches
branches.then: error 'Missing-enrollment diff for program X did not converge after N batches' for that program
its error is collected and the loop moves on to the remaining programs; all errors are joined at the end

steps.title: Enroll the batch idempotently
steps.detail: The diff can go stale between list and enroll (a staff or self-serve enrollment landing first) and an activity retry can re-insert rows from a partially applied batch. Both are safe because the insert skips already-enrolled pairs. Participants a staff member removed from a program keep an enrollment row with status UNENROLLED, so the diff excludes them and they stay removed.

outcomes.meaning: Every participant is enrolled in every approved program it was missing, so no payout run can fail on a missing (participant, program) enrollment.
outcomes.rollback: None; only missing enrollments are created and UNENROLLED participants are left alone.

failureHandling: Activity timeouts are deliberately short (1m StartToClose, 30m ScheduleToClose): a persistently failing small DB query must eventually return an error so the per-program loop can record it and move on rather than retrying forever.
Per-program errors are joined, so one bad program does not block the rest.

workflows.name: StablecoinRewardsRefreshAssetRates

trigger.detail: Temporal schedule stablecoin-rewards-refresh-asset-rates-cron, daily at 17:00 UTC, deliberately after the upstream EFFR and Ethena sheet refresh. Like the enrollment cron it is created imperatively by SetSchedule in every worker at startup.

workflows.timeout: no workflow timeout; the single activity uses a 24h StartToClose timeout
workflows.summary: One-activity workflow that reads the precomputed effective reward rate per stablecoin from a BigQuery reporting table and upserts it into asset_rates, stamped with the as-of date taken from the deterministic workflow clock.

steps.title: Stamp AsOfDate from the workflow clock
steps.detail: req.AsOfDate is set to workflow.Now(ctx).UTC(), not the activity wall clock, so a retried or backfilled activity that crosses 00:00 UTC still writes under the date the workflow started. Using only the deterministic clock is also what keeps the workflow safe for the replay-compatibility test.

steps.title: Query the rates reporting table
steps.detail: RefreshAssetRates reads asset_type_id, rate_type, rate_modifier, source_rate and effective_rate from anc-global-analytics.stables_yield.rpt_stables_yield_asset_rates (overridable via STABLECOIN_REWARDS_ASSET_RATES_TABLE, whose value is regex-validated and falls back to the default when malformed). The reporting table already computes the top-tier effective rate per asset, so this is a straight read. Valid rate types are EFFR, ETHENA_SHEET and ISSUER_LESS. Development and local runs use the fake provider and never touch the table.

branches.when: a row is missing asset_type_id, carries an unknown rate_type, or has a null or unparseable rate_modifier, source_rate or effective_rate
branches.then: that row is skipped with a warning and the asset keeps its last-good stored rate; other assets still refresh

steps.title: Upsert with last-good semantics
steps.detail: On a BigQuery failure the refresher writes nothing and lets Temporal retry; if the query returns no valid rows it logs a warning and does not touch the table. Only a non-empty result set is upserted into stablecoinrewards.asset_rates, and the count of upserted rows is returned. GetLatestAssetRates and the stablecoinAssetRates GraphQL field read from that table, so a bad upstream day shows yesterday rate rather than nothing.

branches.then: no write, activity error, Temporal retries
warning 'BigQuery returned no valid rows; keeping last-good rates', no write, run succeeds

outcomes.meaning: asset_rates holds today reference and effective rate for every asset that had a valid row.
outcomes.rollback: Not applicable. Rows are upserted per asset, so a partial refresh leaves the remaining assets on their last-good values.

failureHandling: Last-good semantics at three levels: skip a bad row, skip an empty result set, write nothing on a query error.
Covered by the replay-compatibility test (internal/temporal/workflow_compatibility_test.go) alongside the other workflows.

workflows.name: Auto-pause on a suspicious bridge event

trigger.detail: A Pause RPC arriving on the internal gRPC control port, sent by Botón's Temporal PauseAuthorizer activity after its bridge-event evaluation returns ShouldPause.

workflows.summary: The kill switch for LayerZero bridging. Botón classifies a monitored bridge event, decides it warrants stopping the DVN, and calls Pause on the authorizer's control port; the authorizer then stops signing everything until someone unpauses it. This is the whole of bridgingauthorizer's external brake — the authorizer does not decide to stop on its own.

steps.title: Botón evaluates the bridge event and reaches a pause verdict
steps.detail: Everything before the RPC happens in Botón, not here: Hexagate posts a signed webhook, Botón starts a Temporal workflow keyed on txHash + eventID, resolves the contract address and chain against the lzconfig-derived BridgeContractRegistry, parses the event name, and looks the (contract, event) pair up in its classification matrix to produce a verdict of {monitoring-plan case, tier T0/T1, blast radius, shouldPage, shouldPause}. Test-token deployments are gated out of auto-pause entirely, because pause is global and would freeze production lanes. For the full evaluation — the registry lookup, the classification matrix, the test-token gating and the ANCHOR_OVERRIDE_PAUSE_BRIDGE_ENABLED override — read the boton-bridge-event-evaluation workflow. From this point on the steps are told from the authorizer's own perspective.

branches.then: no RPC is ever sent; the authorizer keeps signing and never learns the event happened
Botón runs its PauseAuthorizer activity, concurrently with paging via incident.io

steps.title: Botón's PauseAuthorizer activity dials the control port and sends Pause{reason}
steps.detail: The activity uses the vendored client in source/go/lib/protobufs/bridgingauthorizerproto. The connection is plaintext gRPC (grpcutil.CreateGRPCConnectionWithoutTLS) to the location in ANCHOR_BRIDGING_AUTHORIZER_LOCATION, which is bridgingauthorizer.stablecoins:9091 in the deployed environments. The reason string is the human-readable bridge-event alert title, the same text used on the incident.io page, so whoever later reads GetPauseState sees why bridging stopped. Botón is fail-closed on wiring and fail-open on actuation: with ANCHOR_BRIDGING_AUTHORIZER_REQUIRED true (the default) it refuses to boot unless the client connects within a 5-second Ready wait, but if the client is nil at actuation time it only logs a warning and returns success — the pause silently does not happen. Whether the authorizer authorizes this caller at all is unconfirmed (gap-ba-plaintext-control-plane).

steps.title: The authorizer stops signing, globally
steps.detail: Pause stops all signing. There is no per-token and no per-pathway scope in v1 — this is a deliberate simplification, with per-pathway pause tracked as a follow-up. One suspicious event on one lane therefore halts bridging for every token on every chain. That bluntness is exactly why Botón gates test-token deployments out of auto-pause.

steps.title: The pause is recorded with a reason, an actor and a timestamp
steps.detail: GetPauseState later returns {paused, reason, actor, paused_at_unix}, so the authorizer must retain all four. Where and how it retains them is UNCONFIRMED from this repo: there is no database instance, schema, migration or KMS reference for bridgingauthorizer anywhere in the monorepo, so whether the pause state sits in a database, in memory, or somewhere else — and therefore whether it survives a pod restart — cannot be answered here. See gap-ba-internals-unconfirmed.

steps.title: Re-pausing is idempotent and records the newer reason
steps.detail: Pausing while already paused does not stack pauses or error; it records the new reason against the same active pause. This matters because Temporal retries the PauseAuthorizer activity, and because a cascade of related bridge events can each independently reach a pause verdict. The practical consequence is that after a burst, GetPauseState shows the reason from the last event to arrive, not the first — the alert history in incident.io is the record of what actually fired.

steps.title: The public REST signing path refuses while paused
steps.detail: With the pause in place, the sign-only REST API on the public edge stops attesting packets, which is the whole point of the switch. The exact refusal behaviour — status code, error body, whether in-flight attestations complete — is UNCONFIRMED: the REST surface is implemented in anchorstablecoins/issuance-systems and is not readable from this repo. See gap-ba-internals-unconfirmed.

steps.title: The authorizer is unreachable when Botón tries to pause
steps.detail: If the Pause RPC errors, the adapter logs at error level with the reason, tx hash and event ID, and propagates the failure so Temporal retries the activity within its ScheduleToCloseTimeout. The separate and more dangerous case is a nil client — Botón running without authorizer wiring — where the pause is downgraded to a warning log and the activity reports success. Paging is unaffected either way, because PageBridgeEvent and PauseAuthorizer run concurrently, so a human still gets woken even when the automated brake fails.

branches.then: error log plus Temporal retry; the DependencyAuthorizer/Pause metric records the failure
warning log only, activity succeeds, bridging is NOT paused

outcomes.meaning: The authorizer has stopped signing all LayerZero packets and GetPauseState reports paused with the alert title as its reason.
outcomes.rollback: Nothing on-chain is undone: packets already attested stay attested and bridges already in flight are not reversed. Pausing only prevents future attestations. Clearing it requires an explicit Unpause call (see ba-manual-control) — the pause never expires on its own, and nothing in this monorepo lifts it.

outcomes.meaning: The evaluation did not call for a pause, or the call failed against a nil client, and signing continues.
outcomes.rollback: Not applicable.

failureHandling: Botón fail-closed on wiring: ANCHOR_BRIDGING_AUTHORIZER_REQUIRED defaults to true, and boot fails unless the gRPC channel reaches Ready within 5 seconds. It is set to false only for local development.
Botón fail-open on actuation: a nil authorizer client turns the pause into a warning log while the activity still reports success.
Paging and pausing are launched concurrently, so a failure in one does not suppress the other.
versionMarkers: The service was renamed from PauseControl to BridgingAuthorizer (STA-1087).
Global-only pause is a v1 simplification; per-pathway pause is a follow-up.
The Botón-side typed client was added by STA-1230.
